Easy to use and the app has found every food I have entered so far. Down 30 pounds so far in less than 3 months so hard to argue with the results.
It's a very helpful tool for weight loss. The downside is when you forget to log in for a day then all the data from the previous days is gone. I'll be upgrading to the premium version soon.

Update: Thank you for the quick response in restoring the Recipe manager prior to the recent update. Everything seems to be working well again, and my Notes on the recipe cards are intact. Keep up the amazing work on this helpful and informative app!

I'm on a Low Calorie diet, and my doctor recommended me to download the app. It's helped me so much keeping track of the calories. And after 8 days, I dropped 12lbs. But, I love that I can keep track of everything.
I LOVE this app. It's so fun to use and definitely helps me stay motivated through intermittent reinforcement. I've lost a little over 3.5 lbs so far and it's the first week.

I was completely disappointed with this app and cancelled it last year. My request was not honored and they charged me for another year. Again they said my subscription was cancelled. I did not receive any info about a refund. I WOULD NOT RECOMMEND THIS PROGRAM.
I bought the subscription and to be honest the app is not what I was looking for as far as breakdowns of calories macros ect how do I ask for refund i have only used it less than 1 month.

I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS AP!!! Beware unintentional upgrade. $30 per year is ridiculous. Update - I reached out as suggested. Lose-It denied refund because I was outside 5 weeks. So sorry I didn't meet their unpublished timeline. These folks depleted my Google Play account. BUYER BEWARE...

Recent update sucks!! You can't add from a previous meal and update without going into the nutrients plus once you've logged the meal it calculates your remaining calories over the breakfast lunch dinner snack so you don't see the total calories for each remaining meal
this App provides an all encompassing weightloss journey in line with Weight Watchers only cheaper even if you do pay for it which is not absolutely necessary but does provide a few extra facets.

Ive been using this all daily for probably 8 months now and its helped me lose 20 pounds. I am the kind of person who loves to track things, which is exactly what this app is all about. Highly recommend.
Does everything youd expect, even track such things as wster intake and sleep, which are important to weight loss. Has trouble sesrching for certain foods and the settings are very limited.
I really like the app for the most part, but the notifications are awful. It constantly nags me to track meals that I've already entered for the day.
love this app! my favorite thing about it is that you put in all of your info and it automatically calculates your TDEE. Also you can look up any food item if you forget to scan the barcode!

Switched from MFP and this app is so much better. The barcode scanner alone is extremely helpful! Few things I think would help. 1. If after completing the day, there could be a projection of where you'll be after so long if you stay doing this day with activity, food, water, etc. 2. When selecting foods, you could select multiple at once instead of going in and out of the menu options. 3. If you could add progress pictures in with your weight and then do a comparison after so many months.

This is the best app I've found for including all the vitamins and minerals in the nutritional data and for showing the sources for food items (such as USDA). However, the ads are so frustrating because they pop up right in the middle of the screen and stay there when you scroll down. Also, it would be nice to be able to edit the sodium content for what you personally used, and to have the calories info that's at the top in a separate section instead so it doesn't take up so much screen space.

I love this app! Coming from MFP app it was a bit of an adjustment because you get so much more information, so a little overwhelming at first. Once I was able to figure all that out it has truly been the best app for macro and micro counting. I love that you can scan the label and if not there you can take a picture and it auto loads into the system! I love that you can create your own recipes, so helpful when you cook from scratch. Honestly, I can't say enough about this app!

Downgraded from 5 to 3 stars. Started showing full page ads. I don't object to ads. It's the full page ads that take over the screen that I object to. I am not agaist at paying for the app also, as I used the full paid service for awhile until I didn't find it useful anymore. The intrusion of full page ads has me searching for a new tracking app.

Not a hoax, I have done so many calories counters. And all of them end in not free stuff you kinda want. Which is fine. It's a business..but the stuff I need on this is accurate and free. Plus all the micros, and it links to Samsung health and Google fit for free. In my opinion, lifesum and MFP. Whole not had apps. The basics you have to pay for. So not with this. Give it a shot 😊. I didn't get paid to make this comment. I just don't mind supporting something that works. Cheers

The best tracking app available! If you're interested in your overall health beyond how many calories and macro nutrients you consume, this app if for you! It tracks the lion's share of important nutrients and minerals in addition to the macro nutrients. It tells you calories consumed vs calories burned (taking into account the calories you burn just by existing). The icing is I have yet to type in a food that wasn't listed, and only two items I've scanned were missing. LOVE this app!

does what i need it to do, might go to plus some day we will see. definitely replaced MFP Update: Started a gold trial, so far so good. I import recipes from the meal prep manual site, which is far easier than having to enter things manually. I basically meal prep everything, so it works out. If you are serious about counting calories and knowing what you're eating, cronometer is worth it. The secret to gaining/losing weight is manipulating your calorie intake.

I installed this app because I liked that it records micronutrients, however, the app is too buggy to be useful. Multiple times I added food items that never got added to my summary. For this reason, it was impossible to actually track nutrient content. Additionally, so many features of the app are gold status only, thereby making the free version not all that useful. Great idea, but buggy and not well executed.

This app is just not as user friendly or visually appealing as MyFitness Pal unfortunately. I have been tracking macros for many years. I tried the Gold version of the app on the recommendation that this app is more accurate and all entries are verified. I liked the ease of entering a recipe. That function seems to be more efficient. However, the way the macros and calories are listed in your Diary are hard to understand. It's difficult to determine what macros you have left.

UPDATED: Dev team replied to me a few days later saying there were tech issues the day I signed up but that it was fixed. I gave Cronometer another try and have been using it for 2 weeks with 0 issues and IT'S AWESOME. Barcode scanner is quick and accurate, database has almost everything I need. Only features I really miss in the free vsn are meal grouping & more restaurant meal options, but pretty easy to live w/o. I wish the plans had a free trial, but pricing is more reasonable than MFP.

I've used a few food tracking apps, & this one is my favorite. I appreciate the detailed nutrition breakdown (and that the macronutrient info isn't behind a pay wall), the easy user interface, & the customizability. The food database is good quality. I've only found the occasional item that doesn't quite match the nutrition label, & it's easy to add an edited copy to my food diary. The one function I'd love for the developers to add is a way to add multiple foods at once. Edit: Multi-add exists!

I've used MFP for myself for years. Recently started using Calorie King to count carbs for my child's T1 Diabetes, until I heard about Chronometer. I'll never go back! I love this app. The amount of info in the free version is wonderful. Can always find the food I need, information is correct and can usually find the units of measure that I want, too. Also has much better choices for exercise than MFP, for instance, playing basketball or "casual shooting baskets".

I am so grateful to finally find a food tracking app that accounts for pregnancy and breastfeeding. I can now safely count calories and nutrients and knowing my accurace goals and macros. Highly recommend for all users, especially breastfeeding moms who are looking to stay on target nutrition wise and lose weight. The barcode scanner is included in the free version of the app with is 5 star! Most apps charge extra for that. It does have some delays occasionally.

I have used many food calculator apps, but Cronometer is my favorite and the only one I will ever use again. I love how easy it is, and most importantly shows how many minerals and nutrients I am consuming and if I hit my daily intake. I just had to write this review after I saw "Barre" was in the exercises. I was trying to find out how many calories I burned online after that workout and to my surprise you guy already had it 😊 thanks!

I have really been enjoying Cronometer! It makes my calorie counting so much easier. Their database of foods is robust and adding food they don't have registered is made quick and simple with image recognition. Their widgets are simple and cute and their support team is quick to respond to issues. Overall my favorite app for calorie counting so far!

**Important update** Customer service is outstanding and quickly responds to issues unlike some other similar apps. Issue was quickly resolved! **End update** Worked great for a month...until today. Now recipes that are added all of a sudden do not show up as an option to be added in the diary. 20 or so recipes had no problems and still appear but I can not see any new recipes, that are added to the recipe list, on the food list. Ruined the whole tracking experience in a single day.

Tracking my macros, activity, and syncing with Woop has been a breeze with this app. One can even track biometrics such as weight. I like that I can input a recipe or meal in and recall it to make tracking easier. You can even scan a barcode on a product to import nutrition info for foods not in the database. I would like the app even more if whole foods were prioritized in a search instead of popular processed foods.

I love this app. I've learned a lot about the food I'm eating (Did you know mandarin oranges are RICH in iron?) and it's helping me pursue a healthier lifestyle. It doesn't give annoying notifications or pop-ups, and the app is still completely sustainable if you choose not to upgrade. It lists out all the vitamins, minerals, etc in my meals, and if I'm low on one, I can click on it and see which foods are full of that particular vitamin. Pretty cool.

Hi! I love this app. I have kidney disease and use it to track certain nutrients. It is really great. Today though it will not open the diary? The circle just keeps spinning. I have tried a force stop but it still will not open. All my foods and recipes are still there, and the graphs. Just no diary. Help please?

Amazing. Detailed metrics and a simple interface make this my favorite nutrition app by far. I'm learning a lot about the foods I put in my body, beyond their macronutrient profile, so that I can better understand how to make healthy choices. The food suggestion feature is genius as well, when you don't have a great idea of how to meet the remaining nutrient goals for the day.

I think this is an amazing app! I've been using calorie counters for a decade now and I'm this has raised my standards so high! I wish there was a way to influence the suggest food section with dietary preferences like vegan/vegetarian/ect(maybe I just haven't found it yet) but that is literally the only possible thing I could think of. Thanks for making it so accessible!

I switched to Cronometer after seeing a recommendation for it in a reddit comment. I was getting really sick of MyFitnessPal being painfully slow so I decided to give it a shot. Cronometer blows all other nutrition trackers out of the water. It's super fast, snappy, has tons of customization and granular detail to your nutrition. Most importantly, the food databases they draw from are phenomenal, and the user submitted foods are curated by staff for accuracy. Give it a try, you won't regret it

I chose this app because I wanted to simply log my food and get an idea of my nutrition levels, rather than try to diet in any specific ways. It's super customizable and easy to use, and has been a major help. Having the progress bars adds a little gamification element, encouraging me to eat something to raise that bar. The best part is the Oracle feature, because it looks at where I'm lacking and makes a suggestion for a specific food.

Overall the app is great. Gave it 4 stars because there are clumsy areas of the UI where there are just too many extra steps. For example, you just had breakfast and took vitamins. Try selecting 6 things and a few vitamins. There's at least 1 annoying extra step that should be removed since this is probably the #1 experience. And yes, you can group foods and that's great but not commonly used unless you eat exactly the same thing daily.

Used to be really good, and it still is to a certain degree. My main issue is that the barcode scanner barely works for me anymore. When I try scanning things, 90% of the time it tells me that it's a new food that I have to enter in or it'll just pop up a list of my most recent foods to choose from. It takes several times scanning my food over and over for it to finally pull up the correct food, and even then, it rarely does.

the app is so easy to use and has a great interface that doesn't look cluttered. they have a wide selection of foods in the database and it's very easy to add your own recipes. I had never found an app in the past that made it easy to track home cooked meals like this. the nutrient tracking is helpful too and i found adding exercise to be easy as well. it's refreshing to see a free app that doesn't bombard you with ads. keep up the great work!!

I'd used MyFitnessPal for years, and it changed how I tracked my calorie intake. But the price increased, and I de used to use the fit it app, since I have my fitbit. Unfortunately, Fitbit didn't have as many foods, and far less macro information. I'd slipped and stopped logging for a year, and noticed my weight plateau. I stumbled on Cronometer, and it's everything MFP was and more. I love the robust reporting, seeing where the nutrition info comes from, and the ability to export as needed.

The best food tracker I have found by far. I love how the app gives such fine-grained data and lets me log supplements. There's a little learning curve because there are so many settings but it's worthwhile to tinker with the app so you can make it a great tool for your personal health goals. I also appreciate how the app can fit many different kinds of health goals, not just weight loss. It's also reasonably priced. I'm a fan!

Great app, I've enjoyed using it. The customer service is great and it is a great way to get an idea of your daily intake. However, every other food app allows you to separate food by meals (breakfast, lunch, etc). Though the nutritional database is amazing, this keeps me from ranking the app any higher. I've maintained a gold membership for two years, but I can't say that it's worth it, as the only benefit I use is separating my meals.

Contrary to the developer's response, I find numerous errors in their nutritional information (differs from the product packaging) & many whole foods aren't present like some of the more exotic fruits & veggies... also, I'm tired of not getting full use of the app when I am doing the work of inputting or correcting data. I had to correct 2 items this morning alone. I'd stop using it but my doc requires the use of this app. I give it a thumbs down.

A great app for keeping track of your nutrient intake and controlling portion sizes! I subscribed to Gold within a couple of months of using the service, and the extra features are a nice addition, but the free service is awesome as well! The one thing I'd like to see with the service is a way to add profiles for families, as I'd like to be sure I'm offering my preschooler enough, but find it silly to make a whole separate account i would have to continuously log in and out of.

I have been using this for years. Its a fantasic app that is user friendly. They have plenty of data on common foods, accurately portraying macros and micros. The barcode scanner is awesome and just typing the food into the libary usually can find what im looking for with just 2-3 letters. It has helped me maintain, decrease and increase calories while giving my body what it needs nutrient wise. Personally has been my favorite app for my food intake above all the other common ones.

I'm new to this whole food allergy thing and I'm still working out the details on exactly which food is the trigger, so my opinion on this app doesn't hold much value at the moment. It's pretty user friendly though, I love that there is a 'how to use app' option in the menu, a lot of apps don't have that option, surprisingly. I'll update my review later when I'm more familiar with keeping track of your food intake. The dev team has done a really good job!

Great app! I got it to track my vitamin intake, and I love that you can track water intake and also modify to add specific nutrients like Beta carotene. There's a really thorough database of store-bought foods, though I sometimes question the nutritional values entered (or not entered) in the app. I'd also love to see more variety of exercises available for tracking. I practice Kundalini yoga which isn't listed in here, so I have to estimate. Aside from these minor things, I highly recommend it!

I've used MFP for about 7 years now. I track my food intake off and on, making sure I stay on track. I got pregnant, had my baby, and habe been breastfeeding for a while now. It's so hard to get specific goals as a breastfeeding mom, and 8 finally found an app to help. I'm overjoyed with all of the micronutrients data and all the diet options. I don't understand how this app is only 4.6. The only thing I miss is the Widget to quickly log food and see my remaining calories.

Exactly what I've been looking for. Excellent list of foods and vitamins. Information available on the free version that every other app hides behind massive subscription paywalls. Because of this, I've decided if I can manage to keep up with it until the first I'll go ahead and pay for it to support the developer and fully invest myself. Great app.

Well I guess I will be the voice of average Joe in the sea of 5 stars. So far (coming from MyFitnessPal) I haven't been very impressed. -Searching for an item at Dunkin' donuts comes up empty. So I had to use MyFitnessPal to look up the item so I can add a custom item in Crono .. lol 10/10. - I don't understand the calories burned diagram is it for the week? - it does not take into account steps taken during a day as excess calories like MyFitnessPal -how do you update your weight ?! +More

I have used several apps for macros/calorie counting and unfortunately I paid for this one so am stuck with it. The biggest problem I have is that so many common eateries/restaurants are not in the app, so you have to put a bunch of work into manually entering food and beverages. Also, the exercises are fairly generic. Why would YOU (yes, the app developers not put chain restaurant foods into your app????). My spouse has the other popular app and I often have to ask her for info.

So far pretty good. Wish it had a water consumtion part Update: The more I've used this app, the more I love it. It took a bit to discover that you add your water just like your food. It is really very easy to use after I played around with it. (They sent me a note) 🙋This app is much more powerful then the one I used in the past and I can set it to my macros for my style of Keto. I wasn't able to have the previous app I used do that. So each day I discover something new. 5 + ⭐

It would be nice to know IN ADVANCE/PRIOR to installing that registration with email is required. Though to a VERY small degree I understand it, I do not believe it's necessary. Entering birthdate is not easy, especially for older people because we have to scroll through every month of the year AND the years to get to our bday. It's ridiculous. How about a simpler input method?! I haven't gotten to the point of using the app yet, but these two factors are not a good start.

The absolute best food tracker out there...period. Plus so much more! There are so many features with this app that make it easy to use. I'm sorry I didn't find this app sooner. I've tried a few other trackers but if it becomes too tedious to use, I'm out. Chronometer makes it very easy. The nutrition, macronutrient details and other information is extensive and quite helpful. I've done my research into Keto and can tell you, this team know what they're doing. I could go on and on. Awesome!

I recently acquired a garmin watch to help me improve my running. The garmin is extremely nice but does not include direct support for calorie counting. I tried some alternatives (inluding the one recommended by Garmin) but as soon as I saw this one, I knew it was the one. It has perfect integration with the garmin, it counts calories in a way that is understandable and the free version is not ugly with ads. Its databases also seem much more solid than the alternatives.

It looks nice, works well, keeps good track of macros. I can't give it 5 stars because the app doesn't allow you to add other data such as daily BP, glucose, and ketone readings, have to do those online in full version. The only reason I paid for gold was the hope I could add that info quickly thru app. Also it would be very helpful to have a multi add in the diary. Great for free version, not worth paying for gold in my opinion.

This app helped me evaluate the foods I've been eating to figure out what has lots of nutrients and what doesn't. It also helped me realize some high-calorie stuff I was eating that was causing me to gain weight. I also like that when I get a craving for something, I can check the app and see if it'll put me above my calorie target. The food database integrated in the app is amazing, it's very rare that I find something missing. Even then, you can scan the label and add it to the database.

Great for tracking nutrition. Better than MFA in my opinion, having used that one for a while. After they got bought by under armor it hasnt been the same. Too bloated. This is the sleek utilitarian tracker with a large enough database for me, and the UPC scanner works well. Incorporate a pedometer/calories-burned feature and you've got pure gold :)

I have just started using, and I agree to another reviewer comenting about how slow it is. Please, just make it faster to add the food. I don't get into the app everytime to check macros, most of the time I'm adding food. That should be the priority. I hate to have to wait 5 seconds for the home screen to load just so I can add a fruit I just ate. Maybe a widget or shortcut that can be added to homescreen that goes directly to adding food, and skips load time? Please.

I've used the app in 2018 and got back on it this year. I love it, it runs smoother than it used to. The only thing that bums me out is that I can not connect my smart watch on it because the app does not support it. Mine's a cheap one though, the app supports most common smart watch brand. I also find it a bit complicated and long to create a new food item. It would be so nice to just take a picture of the nutrition facts label so the app can scan it and convert it (like a credit card).

I have been using the free version of this app, and it's great. My only complaint is the adds they place directly in the middle of the screen, that you cannot remove, and make it virtually impossible to add the correct measurements of your food into the diary. I understand they need the adds to make it free, but they need to make them able to be removed once seen, or move them to a better location.

Almost perfect. Taking photos of nutrition values is intermittent. That is, it returns to the app's home screen (today's entries), instead of of returning to taking the 2nd photo of the package. This occurrs without explanation why it failed and without the option to proceed with manual entry of that custom food. Otherwise, very polished, very impressive.

Cronometer is definitely the best Calorie/Nutrition App I have tried so far. Customer Service is super and even if I double checked the data in the beginning I never found a single error. The Ads were not annoying, actually don't even remember if there were any ;-)) I am only interested in the nutrition part because I primarily eat plantbased and it's important to get all the vitamins and minerals needed. (Have a wish list)

I've been using the free version for about a fortnight now and can't fault it. Previously, I've used MFP - chosen only because of the link with Garmin - but I didn't like it. I decided this year to try a variety of apps to see which suited me best. Cronometer was first on the list to try, and I can't see me ever moving on! What sets this app apart for me is the support via email; not only are responses quick, it's clear that an actual human being has read (& understood) your query! First class.

Excellent app. They seem to have taken into consideration some app related suggestions I did. Helps me keep track of the food that I eat every day. Needs more work content-wise and the process of adding a new product in for yourself is not very intuitive but overall a great experience with adding the products in. Maybe would be a good idea to allow me to create recipes with ingredients that I can then use to re add to other days as I am usually following the same recipes on a weekly basis.

Finally, they added the dark mode 😀 It was the final touch needed to make this application absolutely perfect. Forget MyFitnessPal, if you want accuracy and useful features, use this one instead. I have been using it it for more than a year, only adding NCDB sourced food items to my diary (i.e. scientifically accurate data on 77 nutrients for each item) and I couldn't think of a more useful tool to seriously take care of one's health.

I cannot search foods with their italian name ( can't change language at all ). Most features are locked behind a pay wall of more then 50€ per year... Can't find lots of foods that i eat here in Italy. I heard this app recommended by lots of vegans for some reason, when there are better alternatives. And apparently without an adblock this app has lots of ads. I see this as a cash grab at best. Not worth my time.

Been using Cronometer for years, I have lots of dietary needs because of a condition and it helps me keep track of my nutrients, supplaments, etc. Helpful for reminding me of what foods trigger a flare up. I also use it for keeping track of my biometrics and gives me a good gauge and history of my health and information to help me make better choices. Love Cronometer, doesn't have the same "fitness" branding as other trackers, much more nutrition-oriented. Simple and helpful :)

Really good app, and so simple to track foods, and then barcode scanner works great for everything ive tried so far. HOWEVER, id pay for the premium, if there was a way to track symptoms as well as food intake, to help with IBS and identifying problem foods. Using it again 6 months later, and would like to get premium features, but just dont think its possibly worth £10/month or £51/year... its a great app, but just dont see how they can charge this much.

Great app, and I would love to have a feature "copy to Today (with edit)" so I could easily adjust the amount (similar to when you copy/duplicate an event in Google calendar). Also the ability to add barcode to copied food. It would be very handy when creating a new food with limited nutrition information from the basis of a well described food. And ability to just add macros without adding food. For example I ate something at a restaurant which I estimate at 10g protein, 50g carbs and 20g fat.

This is an absolutely amazing app, especially if you are vegan and try to include every nutrient in your diet. Anyways, since the last update, all of my custom foods&recipes are gone. I cannot see them in the app, but they are still there when I enter the desktop version. How can I sync the information? Update: The Cronometer Support Team helped me solve the problem. This app deserves 5 stars. Thank you! <3

**please see my edit below** This app would be perfect if it had a less obscure water intake tracking function. Otherwise it's awesome. *Edit: I see your response Cronometer team. I'm aware that food water content is added to the total. I was thinking more of an easier UI option to add water intake outside of food consumed. It's also very difficult to see how much water intake you have in general. Seperate UI elements for water intake (as seen in similar apps) would be a huge improvement.

Best app for calorie counting there is! :) They are slowly adding premium features, but none of the core functionality I've ever used has been taken away. Until then, I give this app 5 stars as it does exactly what I want and need it to do. The food library and barcodes are pretty populated with products I buy here in the UK, which you don't get with many US-centric apps.

This app is very good! It can use some adjustments and improvements but overall, it's great! I recommend having a weigh food scale for more accuracy if your using this but overall its optional. It's very nice for your improvement with lifestyle changes. The app never crashes, in my case. My only suggestion is to add more foods and improve the picture reading for nutrition facts; add more info for the different vitamins and have a little more perspective on what we are eating. Thank you!

Still my fave food tracking app. It puts health before weightloss which I love. Being able to track my vitamins, minerals, and amino acids has been really interesting. It has the most comprehensive food list over other apps I've used. Only thing it is missing is a community board, but I find those places rife with misinformation anyway. I tried using only my fibit calorie counter and had to switch back to cronometer! I've linked the two and am much happier now.

Love this app. Been using it for years. I like how the site provides proper nutritional breakdowns- with all the trace elements and minerals. As someone deficient in those, the required nutrition on store brought stuff is not enough. I upgraded to the pro version because if you have decided to not eat processed foods, the pro version allows you to enter the recipes using the full nutrition info. We'll worth it!

This is exactly the app I've been looking for. It is so hard to find an example online of what we actually should eat to meet our nutritional goals, the internet is full of spam. With this app, I can see what I'm eating and what nutrition I'm not getting then actively work each day to change that with a nice easy visual representation. Perfect. 5 stars

Love this app, has really helped me keep track of my macro and micro nutrients as I've moved to a plant based diet. This app also helps working on weight loss and muscle gain, as you can track your calories and also set personalised protein targets. Would love to see kilojoules added, more foods with detailed micro-nutrient data, and some food entries having the errors in their values fixed, but ultimately these criticisms are minor in an otherwise great app.

I'm vegan and doing a keto diet to lose weight and I know nothing (Jon Snow), but this app makes it easy. Easy to build custom recipes, huge food database and the ability to add anything that is not there already. Tracks goals, link to Google Fit so you don't have to add your exercise. You can't go wrong. Well, you can: doughnuts. That's not down to the app though, but it will help you work out the damage.

Although this app is less popular than MyFitnessPal, and therefore has less foods registered, I find it a lot more accurate in terms of measurements and nutrients. Also, the custom recpie/food option is great, and support answers pretty quickly. Overall, could be a little more optimezed(also, I'm really looking forward to that promised offline mode).

Aussie barcodes when scanning in food! I almost gave up finding an app that I could scan in Australian barcodes, this app has nutritional info on everything from woolworths "cook" and "bbq" range to smaller independent/local brands. The free version is functional enough to track the iron and magnesium levels I'm trying to manage using diet, it's perfect for my needs.

Wonderful app, it has everything I wished for. It took me a while to learn how to use it and to migrate more that two years of recipes and custom foods from my Samsung Health. The fact that I can add my supplements, do a micro nutrients check-up, it is amazing, It would be great if there was a way of syncing cronometer with apps from different devices such as smart scales and watches, this would enable automatic update of weight, exercises and sleep metrics recorded on other apps...

I love how easy it is to add foods that are not in the data base, as not all my gluten-free options are. Just take a couple of pictures, done! After disconnecting the other third party apps, my Fitbit data now imports more reasonable numbers (instead of my activity being twice what it should have been). Numbers are now more in line with the sedentary estimate.

Awesome App for tracking your nutrition, activity and have general info about your body. I've been using Cronometer for 4 years and prefer it to MyfitnessPal. Only one thing I wish to be improved is to add more non-US products. Sometimes I can't find the worldwide brands and it causes some inconvenience. Anyways the App is Brilliant for tracking your results!

not too great for European users... - there doesn't seem to be a way to switch serving sizes to metric units. While I can guess the size of a slice of bread in inches, when it comes to fluid ounces, I'm out. - I tried the barcode scanner on a few items, but it didn't have any of those in the DB. I'm therefore left to use the next best item that's in the DB. edit: when creating custom recipes you can't switch between servings bssed/weight bssed serving sizes once it's been saved.

Fantastic! Perfect for those who like to track not just their weight progress but also get detailed info on vitamins and minerals intake. Highly recommend! Easy to use - it has many products listed, but with the option for custom foods and recipes. Features include daily charts and weekly reports on food and activity. Once I reach my target weight, I'd continue using it as I want to built my muscle strength. It kept me accountable about going to the gym 😁 Cannot recommend enough!

Would be good app, but the problem I find is that it works only online, and then it needs to constantly download every single click, and it takes ages. Adds popup straight way, but everything else... It takes about twice the time to log the ingredients of a food than to prepare, cook plus eat it. Will use it for few days to get a picture of calories etc but not worth the time and patience it takes.

In the website it says that it's completely free to use any feature for regular users (not physicians and such). There's a large pay wall in many basic features. And I just did a couple recipes: the text recognition for the food labels is only in English, it wouldn't accept Spanish input. EDIT:Yes, you can add your own recipes, just make sure you're looking for them with the custom label. I find it pretty unintuitive, if that were to be improved it'd be great. Also, fast staff response in review

I have been using Cronometer for a few weeks now, and it's exactly what I've been looking for. Scanning barcodes makes input really simple, and their databases are pretty well rounded. Love seeing the breakdown of different vitamins and minerals that are or are not in what you eat. Helps making lunches and dinners more directed.

This is very good application. I would be ready to subscribe if developer improves two things: 1. Sending data to Garmin Connect (the same as MyFitnessPal). At the moment app can only pull data from Garmin. 2. Widget for review of calories/ nutritients and quick entry. Please make one. It makes life much easier for your users and it shouldn't be hard to implement one.

I've found this (free version) slightly more challenging to get used to the flow within the app (how to use it) compared to competitors, but actually I now prefer it to others I've tried. A nice app and I love the detail with vitamins and minerals. The food database isn't quite as strong as the last app I tried for items I've used, but I hope this will improve in time with use.

Very happy with this app - I use it to keep track of my diet, tracking the nutrients, vitamins and minerals I consume. I have however, found that the vitamins and minerals are not always added in correctly to some foods and I have had to create a few new food listings to add this info into my nutrition diary. Overall though, this is my app of choice, both visually and in use. Compared to some other apps I have tried out, this has been the most helpful in tracking the nutriants in my vegan diet.

I've been using Cronometer for a few weeks now, and I'm impressed how easy it is to get up and running. It's intuitive, and they've done a great job of making it easy to enter your food. This is a game changer for me, helping me understand what foods I should eat, and what portion size. The daily reports show me any nutrient deficiencies, it syncs with my Garmin watch data so it knows how many calories I've burned compared with how many I've consumed. Cronometer just might add years to my life.

This app has changed my life. I started using it a month ago, and tracked my existing (junk-filled) diet in the app. Seeing my excessive caloric consumption and my inability to meet daily nutrition targets seemed to have turned the right gears in my head. I've now reduced my caloric intake to a healthier level, and have increased the amount of wholesome good food in my diet. I feel much better overall and have dropped a few kgs in just a few weeks. Thank you so much!

This a great tool to track your calories and nutrient intake. It may not be 100% accurate but it gives you an idea of what you are consuming. it has helped me take better control of what I consume, and see how my diet and exercises complement each other to achieve my weight goals. Some foods I consume are not on the list of foods but there are work arounds to finding something close to what I am looking for.

Have been eating keto for the past few months. Using macros trying to count the amount of protein, fat and calories I am supposed to have seemed easy enough. Downloaded this app and I was blown away!!! I was doing it all worng for months. Seriously this app will hold you more accountable with what you are putting in your body. Love how you can scan the food once and add it to favorites for later.

I'm a pregnant vegan and so found this app really helpful - i can track my nutritional intakes everyday. Sometimes i wish there were European brands to find via their barcodes as well. It's bit time consuming to track it all during your days, but once you start putting your recipes there and copying items from some previous days, it really saves you a lot of time and become much faster and easier to track all the food. I'm not sure why it doesn't count my intake of iodine from the sea salt tho..

I like this app. They have all the food I am eating referenced with the proper nitritional information. They have all the nutrients but also all the vitamins, etc.. I can connect it with my strava or garmin profile and the app updates with my watch or other garmins. The only downside is that it takes time to register everything (but thats always the case when writting down all the stuff we eat...), but the app is relatively well made on that topic.

I love the app, so I don't have anything to complain about, but the reason I didn't give 5 stars is because the app only shows you the good stuff you consume and none of the bad stuff, like sugars, saturated fat, palm oil, stuff like that. I'm talking about important things like insulin resistance through dieting. It might be that its an impossible feature to add, but if it could be added I would happily give 5 stars with a cherry on top. Well done otherwise!

The app is very useful because I can scan vitamins and track how much nutrition I'm getting. But 2 problems that should be rectified. Users should be able to easily adjust the nutrition content they aim to achieve a day. The protein intake it auto filled for me is like 170g a day!! That's easy too high! And when entering nutrition content it asks for some measurements in IU which is not possible for some vitamins (ex. B12, k2, selenium, chromium)

Pretty good app - I liked that it gave me insight into most nutrients. But that happens only if I am eating primary foods (like broccoli, rice, etc). As soon as I eat a multi-ingredient packaged/grocery food, the data for nutrient intake becomes unreliable. So I actually don't know if my nutrient intake is on target or if I'm deficient. Big drawback for me because that's what I was really hoping for from this app (and BTW the premium version of the app doesn't solve this) :(

This isn't a bad app at all. It does have one major issue for me, though, and that's this, for all of its databases, it has virtually nothing for people living in Japan. I have yet to scan anything (apart from a couple of import foods) that shows up, and while you can add foods, having to add EVERYTHING manually makes the app more of a pain to use than other apps like MyFitnessPal, despite the fact that it's otherwise a much better app. Hopefully they add some Japanese databases soon.

I've been on the keto diet for over 7 months and this app has made it so much easier! The database of food that this app has, contains almost all food from supermarket chains - allowing you to pick the exact foods you eat. Setting macros and targets is also very easy to do in this app compared to others, in my opinion. Basically, at the end of the day this app has made my journey so much better and I am extremely grateful to the developers! Thank you so much!

I have to say I am quite disappointed with the app - it's not to say that it's inherently bad in all regards, quite the contrary. The UI is sleek, and the information is easily accessed. However, the core functionality on a calorie counter app for me is to add calories, and the food database on Cronometer is horrible - I had no luck adding most of the food I looked for, and adding new food is very cumbersome too. So sadly, I have to return to the competition.

This is the best food tracking app I have ever used. So many apps are so ugly, the ads are oppressive, and they have so much baggage attached. Chronometer is beautiful, easy to use, and has so many good features. Even the free version is so solid. The paid version has a lot of extras I don't really need but would be super useful for others (food suggestions, fasting tracker, etc) but I have the paid version because I think it is so good and even the free version would be worth the cost.

Easy to use, good feedback, easy to understand nutrition information and awesome barcode scanner. Missing some customization options and presets, would love to see something other than the American food accosiasions recommendations. It seems that the nutrition data is crowd sourced, which means some foods are not in the database and the barcode scanner won't work for adding the food item you wanted.

Switched from MyFitnessPal after their latest updates and announcements and this is great! Just sad I didn't start on Cronometer sooner, because the reports and macros and micros tracking are much better for me. I want to track to make sure I eat enough, and that I get enough nutrients. Just counting calories isn't what I need. Besides, Cronometer syncs with garmin on the free version, which is the main reason I started using it. The rest is added bonus!

I've been using Cronometer for years now, through many app changes. Love the micronutrient info (literally only reason I use this), dislike the compulsion of the app team to change the way it functions every four months. There's more taps now to add food than there were two years ago when I could just click on the calorie total in the top left instead of having to open a bottom menu first. Still can't change ingredient order in recipes by sliding them around. Needs better user-friendly design.

I struggle a lot with my weight and this really helped me keep track of my calories, nutrition, and water intake. It keeps me where I'm lacking in or where I'm getting too much and which foods have what percentages of nutrition and calories in my recommended intake. Only one thing that bothers me is that ads block content that I need to see to continue which is very annoying, but I like the app so much I just put up with it. It hasn't happened in a while after I pressed 'x' and said blocks conte

I've used it for several years, but the database is just way too small for European products. Maybe 1 in 10 products that I scan is already in the database, and for the rest, automatic nutrition label recognition hasn't been successful one single time. It seems they didn't make it compatible with EU nutrition labels. Entering the nutrition data manually for every single new product that I buy is quite the hassle. Apart from this, older versions of this app are great.

I really like this for tracking food, although there are some gaps in the database. I'd increase the rating if I could track more than 1 person on it; I'd like to track my daughter under the same account too. She is allergic to dairy and milk, so it would be really helpful to ensure she is getting suitable alternatives. The only work around I see is opening another account under a different email address, but then custom recipes wouldn't be available and everything would have to be added twice.

It's the best calorie tracking app on the market, period. Sadly, the UK database is very poor and despite promises of keeping it updated by Cronometer, too many items are missing, hence I don't think UK customers are being treated seriously. You really need someone in the UK who will keep the database updated. Myself, I'm really upset, because Cronometer would have a huge potential on the UK market, which is currently filled with bloated and glittery alternatives.

Great for detail, has in depth accurate figures covering all the micronutrients. Easy to add foods, which are individually ingredients or shop brought items. You have to manually add recipes, so some initial work there, but once done it's fairly quick to log what you eat. It's a little bit dated design wise compared to other simpler apps like My fitness Pal, and takes more clicks to get stuff done. But this is way more In depth. Pre-existing recipes please!

All around easy to use and makes macro counting easy. It can be difficult to find things sometimes. But I'm also writing since the bar code camera stopped working. Now when I open it it is all blurry and therefore doesn't scan barcode. I checked if my camera was the culprit, but on other things it works just fine. Could you please fix this?

Excellent app. Micro-nutrient tracking is enough to set it apart but there is also a rich database (drawing on authoritative sources in addition to customers' contributions). You can edit everything not just on your mobile but also on your large screen and keyboard, through the website. The two sources, mobile app and website, sync immediately to your account. My general impression is that the Cronomoter team have put technical expertise and hard work into a great product.

Overall pretty ok experience. Some issues: - after you log some food, you can't open that log right away. It takes at least a minute. - sometimes I cannot find food I have previously added, even if I've added it to favorites. It still appears if I scan the barcode again. - for Europe it's never able to read the energy details from the package picture automatically. - it should have the option to view the taken picture in parallel while filling in new food. - expensive full membership.

Love this! As someone with eating disorder background I've searched a way to track my health without getting obsessed with calories, and I was tipped that Cronometer is very customizable. Couldn't agree more! It was very easy to leave calories to the background and instead show trackers for fiber, good fats, caffeine and so on. It even allows tracking stuff like sleep and mood. I appreciate the neutrality, the app itself doesn't push weightloss or diets on me. Subbed for a year, this app is IT!

The ads in the free version are buggy. Once they show up on a certain part of the screen, they won't move, that is after changing screens (e.g. going from adding a new food item to the diary to browsing settings, or reports) the ad stays in the same place on the display. It covers the content underneath. EDIT: it would appear re-starting the app oslves this issue. EDIT2: Some products don't display reasonable units or serving sizes, like 350g being the only serving size for some juices.

In general a really good app to use esp coz it's free! I like that you can set your own parameters and calories. Would be good if there was a water tracker. It always takes a fair few seconds for the app to load or to search food, would be good if it was a bit quicker. Some foods I can't search for or be found using the barcode (Australian foods). Would be good if you could input kj in nutritional info instead of only cal. The app could be made a bit cuter like lifesum but generally happy! :)

This is better than other macro- trackers I've used. Love the ability, that when you've completed your daily food diary, you can see what individual items for that day were highest in carbs, fat, proteins, etc which makes monitoring easier. Also not cluttered with lots of other people's duplicates they've entered. Really useful and lots of info you can turn on or off as desired. I haven't yet seen anywhere that you can toggle between kcal and kJ depending on preference.

New update... Still no 'back/undo' button. I do agree it's got a nicer design, but who even uses 'erase all amounts' ? If you press that by mistake, good luck remembering all the 30 items you entered throughout the day. In general a pretty good app in terms of international food choice, it isn't just American shop items. Adding own recipes and sharing with someone is awesome (gold subscription).

Great, I've been able to turn off the calorie target and concentrate on the micronutrients. I'm starting to eat a much more balanced diet, fewer veggies and more potatoes and cocoa 😂 It's been a week and I'm already starting to feel better. Very useful and adjustable tool - I've set all the basic NHS targets because the ones on the app are very hard to meet on a lower calorie diet but the NHS ones are much more achievable.

I am a nutritionist and I have tried the free version of most apps of this kind. Cronometer is, by far, the best one! It has many unique features that you can't find in any other free version. I particularly appreciate the ability to track several micronutrients, and also the fact that you can edit an existing food and create a new one. So useful for people from different countries where known products have differences in percentages! I will definitely try the gold version once I can afford it!

Honestly I can't imagine a better app for logging calories, I've been using it on and off for almost a decade, back when I did a low carb diet. It logs not only the calories but also the macro and micro nutrients and has a long library of foods, to which anyone can add their own. Also the ads in the app are non intrusive. I only wish this was more international as with a Spanish version I would recommend it to my family members. I haven't found one in Spanish that even comes close.

Love love love this app, if only it wasn't so darn slow. Every time you click something it loads for a few seconds, very frustrating when you're trying to put in large amounts of data such as recipes. I love that it gives you a micronutrient breakdown, makes it much easier to focus on health over weight-loss. It also has all the features I need in the free version. Please just make it less clunky!

I tried a few apps like this but Cronometer is really fantastic! Even with the free version there's lots of options, not always easy to find a product but otherwise easy to create and add to favourites. I'm loving to check food details and nutrients I'm getting every day, I realised that an healthy diet is not always a balanced diet. This app helps a lot in finding the needed balance and make better choices. Top

Fantastic app! I have tried many in the past, but Cronometer has brought it to a whole new level. It's simple, yet sophisticated. It has been invaluable for tracking my childs food intake and fat count (metabolic disorder)! You have made our lives so much easier! Question- can we have multiple profiles? I would also like to track my food intake.

Using the free version. Works well with generic foods and for creating your own recipes. Difficult to get accurate info about meals from their nutritional though, which isn't the fault of the app. Biggest issue is when you change your goals, they change historically rather than from that day, i.e. Today I've changed my calorie goal from -250 to -500. Even though I was within my target yesterday it now looks like I missed it by 250cal. Very frustrating.

Really easy to use & syncs with my Fitbit app. Has already helped me improve my diet in the space of one week! So I have just upgraded to the paid for app for useful food suggestions. I was worried that as someone whose had an eating disordered past, this might be triggering. But in my case it's been amazing to look at my food choices based on nutrition rather than calories.

Dec 11 2020. There seems to be bug. When I accidentally hit the "Add Biometric" button, my phone battery drains to 1%. This has happened twice. Please fix this. Otherwise, I love this app. EDIT: It seems it's not you, it's the phone. It happens with any resource heavy app. My phone needs to be plugged in to withstand this. Otherwise, this is still an excellent app, I just don't open it unless my phone is plugged in. EDIT: Jan 1, 2024. Lost the ability to multi-select from past diary entries.

So far love this app, I've searched for a long time for something for counting micronutrients. It really helps to be more mindful of eating. Also opens eyes what is really in deficit. It would be nice to add options of preparation in adding resipies, as baking/frying in oil can affect micronutrients in resipies, but overall it's good help for me.

Love it! A comprehensive approach to all and any of the food I may eat. Includes macro and micro and every other necessary bit of info tracked (and this is the free version). Sooo easy to navigate and link with web page! I have downloaded so many similar apps and couldn't last five minutes, but I have now filled out my profile and logged three days of food diary with this. Yay! A great app for a Keto newbie! Very happy with the free version. Worth a subscription for sure! 😁

I have been using Cronos for about 8 months now. I previously tried several other nutrition tracking apps, but the frustration level was just way too high. The food data bases were mostly next to useless. I am talking about you, M-F-P. Cronos is the best. And the visual exercise tracking section was an unexpected bonus. Worth the paid version and then some. If you are serious about your nutritional tracking, you won't be sorry.

Very slow and now with unskippable adds. The app was ok for a long time as it was definitely more suitable than MyFitnessPal for tracking self cooked stuff. However, everything takes ages to load and the suggestions are highly focused on the British market in terms of standard groceries. I have tried to make it work by simply contributing lots of standard groceries from the German, Austrian, Swiss, Italian and Hungarian market. But now you have unskippable adds so MyFitnessPal is just better.

great and accurate selection of products and foods in the database with the option to add your own recipes using that selection. Provides all the information necessary and the calories calculator is also fairly accurate. The amount of nutrients proposed in the daily goal though is a bit much so its no big deal if you dont reach them. Additionaly is easy to use and the free plan offers enough for the average person.

I really like cronometer and have been using it for months (and 40 pounds). I have two issues that keep me from giving 5 out of 5. Full admission that I am using the free version so it's like looking a gift horse in the mouth. 1. The charts regularly stop working. I track calories and weight and I routinely have to re-set them up as one or both will vanish. 2. The ads are at times overly intrusive. Ads are fine. Video ads that suddenly play with no warning, at full volume, are not ok.

Since the most recent update the UPC scanner is pretty much useless. Other than that, the program works very well. There are issues with ad placement (as in covering half the screen) but exiting and reloading fixes it. I don't have Gold; there are some features/charts that would help, but overall it's overpriced for my needs, so I can't comment on that. That being said, the Free version covers everything the average user (who isn't tracking medical issues or is a non-professional) could need.

This app is amazing. Far beyond anything I've ever had for calorie counting. It literally makes it so easy. It saves your usual foods, you can scan barcodes for quick adding, and when it can't find the item, you take a picture of the nutrition facts, the front of the product, list a name for it and done. That easy. Plus, you "gain" calories for exercise, as in it shows you what you've burned in calories. As someone who hates adding calories on paper, it's a lifesaver.

I like the site and am interested in using this platform, but the ads in the mobile version are entirely too intrusive. They take up a lot of the screen. I looked for a way to purchase an ad-free version but there is only a subscription option. [edit] found the ad-free version! It's not linked within the app itself which seems like an oversight. It would be more intuituve to have an in-app purchase to remove ads, rather than a separate version. The function of the app is great without ads!

Love the app. The only reason I'm not giving it 5 stars is because the search function is weird. It won't find certain items even though I know they are there (by using the barcode scanner). I love that the app is keto friendly and the recently added fasting is great too. Now I can do all in one app instead of using a separate app for tracking the fasting. I like seeing the evolution of the app. Keep it up :)

Chronometer is a great way to see that even though you may eat lots of fruits and vegetables, you could always eat more! Reaching all your micros is not so easy. Being sure you have all your vitamins and minerals with the right balance of macros like fat and protein is challenging to do without an app like chronometer. Thanks to this tool I have been able to stay healthy and feel great, not to mention have fun experimenting with different regimes. Keep adding new and weird foods chronometer!

This is the best food tracking app I've encountered yet and I've been using it on and off for quite a while. Most organized, yet full, database. Extremely easy to add any food items that aren't in the database. Very complete tracking. Lots of connectivity with fitness trackers. It's only become easier and more effective to use as time has gone on and I appreciate that it is a 100% useable app without premium but has those more advanced options as well.

This app is my favourite food/calorie tracker. Most detailed nutrition reports I've seen in any app, with macros, vitamins, minerals, carbs, fats, and proteins, and loads of food options. Any food not in the system is quick to add, and if you eat the same meal often, it's easy to put all the ingredients together in one recipe so next time you eat it, it's only one click. Dark mode is a massive bonus too. The free version is awesome for everything I need, no compromises.

I hate the new look for this app. It's got everything all over the place when you want to add a food to your day instead of giving you the practical overview and letting you see details if you want, but leaves them out if you don't. When you press add food is also doesn't automatically start the cursor in the box for you to type. You have to press it manually. It's very very hard to read the nutrient summary of a food because of the colors, the layout. Ugh. I'll be using the app less honestly

All that I need is available in the free version. Easy to use and plenty of additional data which you have to choice to use or not. I can copy paste my listings from one day to the next and easily add recipes ornew foods to the list. There are some ads that pop up but this doesn't happen very often and they are easily switched off. It's a great tool!

Hands down, the best nutrient tracker I've come across! Only complaint is that it would be nice to have a "most recent" food list, instead of "most frequent". Sometimes you'll buy a new product, say a new type of cheese, and you haven't eaten it enough for it to show up in the "most frequent" list, meaning that you have to scan the barcode EVERY SINGLE TIME you eat it. Ironically, it starts showing up in the "most frequent" list right around the same time that you finish the package.

I much prefer this app to MyFitnessPal, since there is a strong focus on nutrition as opposed to just calories. It's also better in the sense that you can customize the settings based on your food restrictions. One thing that I would like to see is the ability to import online recipes to Cronometer. This would be excellent as it usually take me around 20 minutes to add a recipe to the app, and this can cause quite a bit of frustration.

Love love love this app. Was using Myfitnesspal but was underwhelmed by the available freatures (even if I upgraded to paid). Tried a couple others and stopped immediatly when I found cronometer. It is every thing I need. I love that it shows all the nutrients, and breaks down not just the whole day, but individual items eaten through the day so you can see how different foods impact your vitamin requirements. It even breaks down the different proteins. I no longer need to take supplements to make sure I am reaching my requirements as I can adjust my food intake using this amazing app and be confident I've got it covered. Thank you for creating this wonderful app, and for making the free version full of so many features so that everyone can benefit. It is also easy to add your own recipes, and break them down into serving sizes. So far I have found every food item in the list that I need to be able to add to my diary. Thanks again.

Amazing app! I've tried to use MFP several times over the last few years (simply assuming it's the best), but I've always given up. MFP is just too awkward and time-consuming to mess around with. By chance I gave this bad boy a go, and I cannot tell you how happy I am with the experience. It's so much easier and better than MFP! Subscription is a little bit expensive for me, but the free version is still excellent, and the ads are not too intrusive...

Really like how the app works, when it works. Very slow, lots of bugs,and often have to log out of connected apps to make it work. However lots of useful nutrition info. I like how the recipe section functions. Not as many products in the database as other apps eg myfitnesspal, but more easily accessible information about nutrients. I hope it gets better on the tech side. I have contacted customer support numerous times- they are very helpful and I'm sure they are working on the issues.. slowly

It's an amazing app. I've used it since I started my weight loss journey with keto. It's awesome at tracking macro and micro nutrients. The food database, while not perfect is a LOT better than mfp for example. One improvement I would like to see: in the targets screen, if you click on a certain macro, it takes you to another screen that shows where you got those quantities from (I.e. the 300mg of potassium came 37% from the spinach you ate today, 20% from the mushrooms etc) . But if you added your food as a recipe (say a salad with spinach and mushrooms) it only shows 57% from the salad and does not go into the detail of which ingredients specifically. Other than that, it's an amazing app!

I chose this app because it provides not only macros daily intake but, more importantly for me, vitamins and minerals. The only problem is pre-made foods - they only count the nutritional facts written on the box when there are more to consider. Also difficult to add restaurant foods to the diary for this reason. Still, easy to use, has a wide variety and easy to add my own recipes. Also, diet targets can be personalized.

Overall, it's a fantastic app—the breakdown of nutrients is incredibly helpful to help me manage a chronic illness and ensure I'm getting all the nutrients I need! The only downside is i connected to Samsung Health, thinking it would auto pull in my step count, but it doesn't seem to. I'm not sure where I should look to find out if it's pulling in my Health data or not!

Finally, after several attempts over 4 days, got this up & running. Only persevered due to a personal recommendation received. Have increased rating from 1 to 3. still new to app & still testing. At this stage, looks pretty good. Search results for when adding food are in random order, not in alpha order. Hence too much scrolling required. Not being able to use kj, kilojoules is a nuisance. Help functions are pretty good, but don't always have complete info.

I've been using this app for several years & it's always been good & very useful app for anyone wanting to track their nutrition. While it's got better with each release, it's never been a full replacement for the website... until this latest version. You've really knocked it out of the park this time cronometer! It now does everything except the washing the dishes! Great work! Would give it more than 5 if I could.

Out of all the counting apps i found this one is the best. Items actually scan and easy to add new items if they don't ready for next time. You can change your calorie/macronutrient targets easily without needing to pay which is great! So many others apps didn't scan items or have any options to add them. Even charged money for updating details. This app does not have these issues. Easy to use. Thankyou for making an app for those who need the basics for now with no extra money :)

Easy to use and wonderful! Maybe more educational tools would be nice, but perhaps that comes with buying the subscription--I'm not sure. EDIT: that would be great! Thank you. Some of the education I would like to have would be: -Brief explanations of what each nutritional element does for the body -Lists of the best foods for getting each nutritional element -Explanations of the dangers of over-or under-consuming a nutritional element I suppose some of these might be resolved in premium?

The Best of The Best. I can vouch that this app is the best when it comes to nutrition tracking. And it's free. In all other apps I've used (which is tons), I've found I have to pay inorder to see my omega-3 and other advanced nutritions. But so surprisingly, Cronometer provides all the nutrition tracking FOR FREE. They are truly amazing and I am eternally grateful for the team of this app. You can also add your workouts too. And the data of foods available is so great even for Indian foods.

Disappointing! I really like the app, find it really easy to use and very informative. But and it's a major but, the full screen ads just take the piss quite frankly. And no I don't want to be hooked up with a free trail. If the app was a one time purchase then I would have bought it, but the monthly / yearly subscription is just way too much for what it is. This coupled with the full screen ads I have returned to MyFitnessPal. The free version does everything this does and so much more.

Hands down the best app for tracking macros with one huge flaw....the fast tracker. Its clunky and confusing and simply doesn't work. I start tracking and then go to my home page and its not working, so i start again and nothing. I use Zero and i think you would be better off linking that app. You have an amazing product and i think you need to get busy improving that feature or just remove it. Otherwise 5 stars. Keep up the great work on everything else!

I would give it 5 stars, but the biggest let down for me is there is no way to change it to kilojoules. Which is ridiculous! I am aware most people in my country measure in calories but I personally measure in kilojoules. I have heard other people saying the same thing as well so I'm not the only one. Google Fit gives you the option to change to kilojoules so I can't understand why Chronometer doesn't. I will use a different health & fitness app instead that gives you that option!

Very extensive, gives you a lot of information for free where other apps may not (e.g., MyFitnessPal). The database didn't seem as large as MFP, but the option to take a picture and have it autofill nutrition makes up for it. It struggles for something like takeout but that's a common issue among nutrition trackers. I also found the display/customization to be somewhat lacking. However, it's a great app and I'd definitely recommend.

Great app! Just would be awesome to "fold" a group of items below a label, and also would be great to have an easy way to compare different foods, like nutrients per 100g or per 100kcal. By folding I mean, for example, having a label 'breakfast' and inside that group some items, say cookies and coffee, and with a little arrow on the 'breakfast' label those items would be shown or hidden. Similar to the behavior of the Foods tab, with 'my recipes' and 'my food' that can be folded/collapsed.

So I've been using MFP for about 15weeks now and it lacked the ability to change values. It didn't even let you track things like Vitamine D, (crucial when living the arctic) or even Omega3. I have no words... This app however, Cronometer, is SO much better! It actually let you keep track of what you want to keep track of. Their DB doesn't have all my local items, probably because of low usage around me. But I don't mind since I prefer to add it myself. For now, this gets a rare 5 stars

Everything is pretty good. Just a couple small things. It would be nice if when you need to manually type in a food item that the list would populate with calories. You have to click on each item to see the calories. Also the arrows to change between dates would be nice on each side of the date. Instead of both on the left side. It's just a small issue though and for some reason I can't stop going to the right side of the date looking for the arrow to switch to the next day every time lol.

This is probably the best app for tracking calories and macros. The information is accurate for the most part and the ads for the free version are not intrusive. The free version already offers the majority of what you need unlike other calorie counting apps. As long as they don't charge for basic functions in the future it's worth trying out.

Phenomenal app. I can't understate how much it's helped me. The easy access to high quality data has taken nutrition from guesswork to precision for me, and really helped me understand exactly how many misconceptions I had. I've lost 30 pounds in three and a half months, and feel better and am eating better than I ever have!

You can use a lot of the features included with this app for free, excluding just a static ad placement that isn't obtrusive. There is a surprising amount of data that is displayed in various ways once you start inputting information and meal items. I really like being able to scan barcodes to autofill item data. I was able to sync data from my galaxy watch 3 with it as well. I ended up subscribing to try out the gold features and because I've been using this every day and find it very helpful.

Very good app, but there are some flaws I'm having like (When the search is difficult because there are strange codes), But on the one hand, this application has its own advantages compared to other applications, namely being able to do tracking on micro nutrients, Like Vitamins & Minerals very well. then you can edit the food data if it is deemed less accurate for personal use. I LOVE IT SO MUCH

Great app but have to look elsewhere. I eat similar foods daily and unfortunately it deletes all my entries daily. It's annoying have to enter the same foods everyday or if I want to check something in my diet. Not sure why I do not have the choice to keep my entries ongoing then if I change my Cerial for the day for example I delete the current cerial and add the new one. Nice and easy. Evey thing else is amazing. I've emailed a few times they give an option that doesn't really help

Very handy app and pretty easy to get started with. Very customisable for my food tracking use. Has a surprisingly vast array of foods in its database. I'm in Ireland and search stuff I get in my supermarket and 80% of the time the exact product is there! Haven't gotten around to seeing whether I need the paid version. Ads aren't that obtrusive anyway. Good interface and a pro layout..5 stars..

The app is pretty good, I really like that it gives such a detailed description of the nutrients. My only problem is that it doesn't give an option for me to see kilojoules instead of calories. Kilojoules is the standard where I live and I don't like having to do conversions every time I look at a label in store.

I love this app and have been using it for years. It really helped me as a new vegan to ensure I was getting all of the essential macro and micro nutrients, and not deficient in anything. Also helpful to set and track weight goals, and has the option of selecting various different diets (80-10-10, paleo, etc), or customizing your own.

Great app that gives a clear and comprehensive picture of your daily nutrition! The only observed possible drawback after a week of usage is that it apparently doesn't take into account the vitamin C loss in cooked foods (50% or more). This is probably an issue of some of the databases used. Also, missing information for database items is considered as zero content (e.g. calcium in Yoplait petit suisse). So a great feature would be to add an average value for similar foods, instead of zero.

Cronometer is an excellent guide and support tool for improving any health issues, ex Cholesterol, diabetes, weight loss/control and exercising to avoid medications. I've learned the importance of keeping track of macros, micros, when I need to eat more or less, change my food choices or exercise more to meet my goals. Cronometer is one of those rare finds that is truly practical. I have recommended it to those who say they get discouraged when they try to live a healthier lifestyle.

Everything was wonderful, I paid for the ad free version on the app. I have been using it sinch mid March. This morning, I wake up to an update which changed all of that. Now I have ads. And the only way to get rid of them is to upgrade to gold. No thank you. Seems highly dishonest. I either want no ads like I was promised when I paid for the app, or I want my money back.

I was a long time MFP user. Researched a few alternatives now and Chronometer came up on top. I really quite like it, despite the lack of the basic breakfast, lunch, dinner grouping in the free plan. The one reduced star is due to the lack of a data export option. I'm surprised this is even allowed in view of GDPR law in the EU.

Excellent food tracker. It gives detailed breakdowns of your macro nutrients as well as your vitamins and minerals. I was able to identify areas I wasn't getting certain nutrients and modify my diet to correct it. The default food library isn't as exhaustive as My Fitness Pal but the information is more accurate and it's very easy to add new foods yourself and the more detailed vitamin/mineral breakdown gives Cronometer the edge over MFP in my books. I

I love this app. I originally downloaded it to track my salt and potassium intake because of high blood pressure, but tracking all my other micronutrients is helpful. It took me a few days to get the hang of all the features and now that I'm used to it, it's really easy to use. I did keto for a while and it tracks macronutrients too so it was very useful. I didn't need to pay for a subscription because it already does everything I need and there aren't too many intrusive ads.

Marginal as an app. Search for foods to insert in diary is hit and miss. Entries are not standardized by brand or venue, so in many cases you end up making things up, which defeats the purpose of the app. Unfortunate plugging for 'gold' is also annoying given the diary problems which tell me an upgrade would be a waste. Dropped another point for their pointless answer to my review. Also, while the link to Google fit is okay, it does not recognize snow shoveling.

I love this app. I can't believe all the features it includes and the research that must have gone into it. I'm learning so much about what's healthy - like potatoes(!!)- and how to optimize my health. I've been using it for only 2 weeks and I'm noticing a difference in both my mood and my arthritis. Well done, team Cronometer.

I like this app. I've been trying and testing out other apps as an alternative to fitness pal and so for this has been the best option. Easy to use and has a good selection of food items in the data base that I don't have to add. I would like to see what's eaten divided up into breakfast,lunch,dinner sections but it's a good app.

One UI change would make this a 5 star review. Make tracking weight more intuitive and simple! I have to pass through several screens to do it: tap the big red plus button, tap "Add Biometrics" and search for "weight". Adding weight should appear as an option as soon as I tap the big red plus button! For a calorie counting app tracking weight should be as intuitive and simple as tracking food!

Best nutrition-related app I've used.    Extremely detailed, highly customisable, it can be tailored to anyone's need, and it offers the best overview of micronutrients of all the nutrition apps I've used - they tend to focus on macronutrients.
