User interface is very nice and easy to use, the app itself is very simple to use but it also offers complex data - and they constantly optimise the app and add features.  Quickly subscribed to the gold membership - I plan on using the app/website daily!  Easily see what nutrients you need on a daily basis, interesting graphs, the Food Oracle feature is brilliant - it suggest foods to eat to gain missing nutrients.   You can select foods from a huge, growing database, and you can also add foods (to a personal bank, or the official database, once it is curated)  There's also a very neat feature where you can add recipes, and it'll calculate all the nutrients based on the ingredients you mix in  Brilliant app.

I love this app it is the best I have found for tracking all your daily nutrients and seems they have added an option for saving meals in the free version which is a great time saver !! I've been using this app for over 2 years and it has honestly helped me so much in improving my understanding of food and how to organise my own diet. Thank you ! I would highly recommend to anyone who needs to track their diet for health reasons especially.

Best one I could find still, but 3 main annoyances: 1. If you don't restart the app (and clear it from history) it doesn't update what "today" is. can even cause bugged entries 2. Offline entries are impossible. Just allow users to make entries offline that will be synced next time they login. Even if they can't search for foods properly etc 3. The 12 digit passwords are annoying, but the reason you gave makes sense. upped to 4 stars

Awesome product with great features. A few things I'd like to have/change on top of an API(!!!): - since the information it provides can be quite overwhelming, I haven't figured out a way to customise the UI for myself when I log in and want to see how I'm doing that day related to my daily goals/limitations - I can't figure out a way to add custom nutrition information that I care about that the software doesn't have. - be more user friendly and don't overload with information users don't need

This app does one thing and does it well. It has detailed nutritional information and sensible caloric deficit calculation. The data visualisation is clear and helpful. It supports biometrica like bodyfat percentage. It's not trying to be a social media app in that it doesn't encourage you to share photos of your food, which is great. I used to calculate macronutrients using a spreadsheet and this feels like a more more efficient way of achieving the same thing, without any extra frills.

I cook all my food and worried I'm not getting the right nutrient balance and this app has been educational! I got premium for the "suggest food" option bc I was struggling to meet a lot of nutrients, but they are absolutely nonsensical. I meet my vit K needs, yet it gives me recipes with +400% vit K and little else. And there's no way to actually see the details of the suggestions. So they'll get cut off unreadable. I will not continue my premium b/c the one thing I want from it is useless.

Not impressed at all. One more app that if you're not in the US is too much trouble. Tried to add a Canadian Jam and it was so much trouble I no longer interested. I don't have that kind of time for that much work. Had to quit the entire process therefore wasting time. Edit: it scanned everything but let me save nothing. Said I missed naming it. Did that, still didn't let me save.

Just tried this app for the first time. Even something as simple as adding a coffee with cream and sugar was ridiculous. I had to scroll forever to find what I was looking for when searching coffee. Also, after having the app for less than an hour, I've already received a notification trying to get me to upgrade to premium. The price for premium being $12.99/mth has got to be a joke? That's almost triple what other apps like Lose It wants. Ummm it's not Netflix.

Down several pounds and still going. This app has been fundamental in my progression toward achieving my goals. This is the first app I have given a written review of, and, also one of the few I've signed up for a paid membership. The latter is not necessary, everything is already free and available, but I just like it so much that I did so. I recommend this app for anyone on the path to better health and desirable weight. I live in Australia and have had no issues with nutritional information

Very informative but not very user friendly. I changed my macros to suit my daily cal intake (which I had to google how to do) and for some reason on my diary page it still has the incorrect amount of daily cals. And I have no idea if my burnt cals is being excluded from remaining cals. Probably recommend this app to seasoned people. Not beginner counters. It's a bit to involved.

Used to love this app but now it's slow and the barcode scanner doesn't even work right because my camera's focus becomes locked and is too blurry. Honestly pretty annoying to use now, and some items are straight up wrong with their nutritional info (as in I'm comparing them to a package in front of me and they're off by a lot). Probably will stick to a spreadsheet out of frustration.

Great app design and layout but the database is lacking compared to MyFitnessPal. However, I like that I can manually add products by taking a picture of nutrition facts and the free barcode compared to MyFitnessPal. Love the ease of connecting to device such as my Garmin watch, Fitbit tracker and polar heart rate monitor. Edit: After the using the app for a 3 weeks I love it. The ads are not intrusive though that may vary where you reside and The reports are very useful to help reach goals.

I love this app. Simple to use and doesn't require me to pay to input custom macro targets in gram (please don't ever change this). One suggestion I do have is the addition of body measurements and stats. I currently have to use two apps (this included) to track overall progress for my recomp. I'd definitely pay to be able to do everything in one convenient location.

Best nutrition/calorie tracking app out there. It is far better and more detailed than Lose it or My Fitness Pal. Sadly it takes FOREVER to load. It is very frustrating when my food gets cold while I'm trying to open the app. If the issue is addressed then it will hands down be my app of choice. Until then however I'll be going back to lose it.

Fabulous, the free version is more than adequate for basic calorie tracking, meal planning and recipe planning. The free version tracks weight fat protein carbs fibre water and calories and a big heap of other stuff that I dont bother with. Will accept input of new foods and recipes. I find 99% of the foods I use already in the database.

It's a brilliant app overall but since the last update, it's become very slow to start, it keeps crashing, especially when I'm trying to add new food after scanning an items bar code. I've got the Gold membership and till recently have been very happy. I've cleared the cache, phone junk files etc. I'm not quite sure what else to do.

Most thorough, in-depth nutrition tracker on the market, hands down. If you wanna go deep into analyzing your micronutrient intake and ensuring the correct balance of nutrients, this app is for you. Used the free version for a few years and finally upgraded to gold. Worth every cent! Great app also for professional dieticians, and managing their clients nutrition and biometric data.

Pretty decent app overall, although when adding packaged foods, even if their ingredients are very simple (e.g. Peanut butter that is 100% peanuts), it won't give the BCAA breakdown unless the database specifically has that data entered (which it almost never does). It would be cool if, for products that have clearly marked and quantified ingredients, it applied the additional detailed info where it is not otherwise available.

Best fitness app I've tried so far. Handy as a very general tracker of diet and activity. Unfortunately, the nutritional data and calorific values for exercises aren't always accurate so you have to err on the conservative side when estimating progress toward weight goals and use with other resources. The idea behind it is great so I hope it continues to develope.

I have used MFP for over 10 years now....but recently switched to Cronometer (triggered by the horrendous sync issues of MFP). So far I am really liking it. I do wish you guys were a bit cheaper for the annual sub (for paid users since you are still lacking some things like challenges, friends, and gamification). However, I do like the app a lot. I hope your database grows to MFP levels. Lots of south asian food needs to be added. I am probably going to subscribe to gold for both myself and wife in a few weeks.

This app is very thorough in calculating calories, macros, micros, and so much more. I use the free version, and it has been such a huge help in determining which nutrients I have not been eating enough of. My fitness pal and fitbit food tracking both pale in comparison. I'm very impressed. Thank you so much for making this app available!

Only app I found that doesn't require payment to let you track macros/micros, scan barcodes for products, let you set your own calorie and macro targets to whatever percentages or fixed values you'd like. Also lets you set weight loss/gain goals per week that updates with weight input. If you are willing to dive into the settings it is highly recommended. Has video ads that can last like 10-20 seconds but worth it!

This app is freaking amazing. I love how well their website works, way better system than myfitnesspal. I like how you can make recipes based on the weight and then adding or subtracting water when needed. Myfitnesspal was pretty messy when it came to this and this apps makes it way more simple. I would love to have a visual example of what I'm putting into the diary. I know it's silly, strawberries are strawberries, but being Spanish sometimes translations might not be exact.

App allowed me to lose weight steadily at the rate set in the app. All I had to do was enter daily foods and stay within the calorie target over a weekly averaging period. Since achieving my weight loss goal, I have continued using the app to have ongoing detailed information about nutrient intake. The app has proved that a "whole food plant based" diet (which has normalised my blood pressure and blood lipid levels) meets recommended nutrient intakes and is safe & sustainable in the long term.

I love this app, however, recently whenever I update a quantity on a food item it pushes it to the bottom of the list whereas before it would stay in place. it makes planning meals in advance more frustrating as you then end up having to reorder it again once you've entered the correct weight. Please change this back to how it was before. Edit: thank you so much for fixing the glitch so quickly, this truly is such a wonderful easy to use app. I've tried all the others and this is the best

I've used the webbased version before and liked that. The current app version hides meals you've entered behind a paywall when they're more than 7 days old. This app fails to be what i want it to be, a tracker. I will uninstal and look for a better app. 2 stars because there are some okay features, i just hate having my own data withheld from me.

The app has a potential of being really good, but it is very slow and laggy. If it worked smoothly it would be amazing. It is extremely slow to open it and to add food, so much so that I skip days when I don't have spare 30 minutes just to ad my meals. If this continues I probably won't renew my suspicion.

This app put a spotlight on my low energy problem, highlighting how low my daily fat and omega 3 intake was. Really surprised me, but it was spot on. I feel incredible now, workouts feel better, can challenge myself now in a really good way. The app has a lot of intuitive features that keep pushing me (almost unconsciously) to good, nutrient dense foods to meet those targets. Love it.

Some nice features but I don't like having to logon, I'm disappointed this app works only with wifi/data on. Unfortunately similar apps also require internet connection.I have only installed this because samsung health doesn't have extended vitamin and mineral counts. Also, although I want to increase my weight, I don't want to gain 0.5 kg every week. I want to gain weight a lot slower.

This app is fantastic... It is connected to a great database making it really easy to enter accurate data and get nutritional data in return. The interface is simple easy to use... The free version has a minimal advertisements and I hope that pays for development as I don't use this often enough to warrant or purchase. Can't say enough good things about this app.

I've been using Cronometer for years now and I'm in love. Abundant database with all the micronutrients, app integrations for importing steps and exercise and acurate TDEE calculator on top of that, macro calculator, custom nutrient goal settings, tracking weight, body fat percentage with charts and weekly reports. This app's even got custom food and recipes option and A BROWSER MODE. I couldn't ask for more, yet Cronometer keeps on giving. Hands down my favourite app of all time!

works a treat for counting calories and macros . note that it's more tailored towards the US when reading labels . UK brands have limited coverage , but you can always add your own . I've never personally got a label to read itself using picture function , but it's still amazing for a free app. still using it now .

Awesome tracker all around, but minor features that went missing detract a star. Its a great go-to app for not only calorie tracking, but measuring nutrient profile summeries. Adding a previous foods seems to have a random default measure - ie I go to add milk and it lists 0.2 cup instead of 1. Update - batch adds was turned off in app - turned on and happy again. Having a default measure consistently, or just having the prev measure would be a great fix to adding foods as well!

After a bug a few days in, I was ready to start my quest for the perfect app, again, but the team was extremely helpful and responsive and fixed the issue quickly! I have been looking for an app enabling me the "luxury" to built custom recipes and then using them as ingredients in other recipes; I have to make all my food from scratch, but also need to follow up my intake for health reasons, making usual app with commercial food libraries fairly useless to me. I finally found *the* tool! Thanks!

Great app for tracking your Macro's and Micro's. Its nice with an app that does not try and force a paid version on you, you might get the occasional question if you want to upgrade to gold version but I haven't found it annoying at all. I'm using the free version and loving the app. It also let's me use it both on my phone and on my computer in the browser which is very handy. I can recommend this app if you want to gain or loose weight or even just to track daily intake. 5/5 Grewt app!

Wow.. this really surprised me with how bad it was.. especially after the commitment they force u to make just to sign up.. during that process, I thought this would have to be amazing to be worth it.. but it wasn't.. couldn't even enter the desired amount of grams for my carrot.. the app is just ad infested, premium suggestive, and just a clumsy Interface

Overall, a decent app but there's a deal-breaker for me. The database is well-equipped and frequently updated, which is a huge plus. However, the app keeps logging me out, usually after 2 days and sometimes randomly. More often than not that puts me off using it completely and I turn to alternatives.

I'm broke yet I choose this subscription over most other things, I don't care all that much about calorie counting but I eat a much more balanced diet by entering the food I have eaten or am planning to then use the food suggestion part to tell me what to eat to best meet my micronutrient goals. Also I thought of something that would make my experience better half an hour ago and used the feedback tab to mention it, just got an email from an actual person on how to get what I want!

This is the only app that tracks so many nutrients. It has a wide database food items that you can scan or photograph the back of pack and autofill, failing that you may need to input. It has ketogenic setting, intermittent fasting, set your own macros, w/loss goals nutrient targets. takes a bit of hard work/study to get full use but its comprehensive. Premium paid sub not needed for all of that. Good tool to analyse if your diet or a meal falls short.

Best meal tracker I have ever used. Simple, lots of food options and valuable information about them, also thr ability to create meals and know each nutrient they have. I can track my calories and nutrients for every product I consume so I can plan better. I have been using for more than a week and saw only one ad. Well done!

I've tried a lot of calorie tracking apps! This one is my top pick. It has a simple yet powerful user interface . As a developer myself, I can say this is very polished. Although the food database may not be as many as others, this has curated ones. The autofill for nutritional facts is very cool! This version is a step-up from the older versions before. Adding a food before was so tedious and strict, but now it became friendly for lax users and became even better for meticulous ones. Kudos!

Best app! It definitely helps to manage weight lost. It integrates with to your smart watch device (in my case Fitbit) and is interesting to see after exercise activity how the total amount of colaries allowed increased. The detailed breakdown of food including net carb (which help to monitor blood sugar level) is accurate and amazing. Best of all, if an food item is not in the database you can simply take 2 pictures on the package and submit. Everything is so technologically integrated.

i've only been using it for a little while, but it's good and useful. it is a bit limited when it comes to not American foods, nearly every time i try to scan something it's a new food, (which isn't bad, but slightly frustrating when you're trying to quickly use the app to have to input all this data) but beyond that very useful!

App is clear, well designed and to the point. Adds are minimalistoc and non-intrusive. Only thing in need for improvement is the food search function. If I made dinner without one of their recipies and want to just fill in, say pasta, it will always find recipies with pasta instead of just dried of fresh pasta. Same goes for just about any seperate item (bread, fruits ect). Other then that, good app!

I had to delete this after one days use...to be replaced by the ad free version because it's worth it! This is such a brilliant program and I'll be a casual user but it gives me all the info I need readily accessible unlike some of the other nutrition tracking apps like MFP. Syncs perfectly with my Garmin connect app too so it's all seamless. Ads aren't obtrusive so feel free to use the free version- i just thought if throw a few dollars in support of an essential keto/low carb tool. Thanks.

Really good with one major drawback. No option to divide food into separate meals I pay - why? I generally sit each evening to plan my food for the next day - I don't plan it in chronological order, I add stuff as I think of it. MFP, LifeSum etc. enable this for free, why not this app? It is quite hard to remember what food I'd planned to eat with which meal if it's all on one long list! Otherwise, love it. Detailed nutrition data - amazing. Fix the division of meals issue & it will be 5 stars!

Lots of great free features all easy to use. Syncs with my Garmin and all of the data (calories consumed, calories burned, macros etc) is clearly laid out and easy to understand. Everything I need is all in one place! When it comes to ads, most of them are small banners that you don't even notice. I can count the number of pop up ads I've gotten on one hand, probably. My one suggestion would be to make it easier to add water. I can do it through food, but a quick add would be very handy :)

Great app! I love it. Being able to create food lists, recipes, and meals are so easy, and I know exactly how many calories, fats and carbs I am consuming every day. I am a type 1 diabetic, and since I have been using this app, my sugar levels have been amazing. I've also lost 10lbs in 4 weeks.

This has honestly revolutionised my health and my life. I've been keto and careful with my diet for years. I'm also very careful about salt because I have high blood pressure. I used the free version of the app for a while but switched to the paid version mostly, to be honest, to support the company because I thin it's such a great product. It's a bit of added work in your life, but so is keeping a budget. In both cases - TOTALLY worth the effort!

I was really Impressed with how many foods are already loaded, especially ones from Australia as many times you have to set them up. also is quite easy to set new foods, or recipes up even with the free version. I love being able to see where I'm at with hitting my macros. provides great insight to my food intake.

Excellent app. It helps massively with carb counting for type 1 diabetes and has a wide array of features without seeming bloated. Easy to use, integrates effectively with Google Fit. They've also got very responsive customer service and make it very easy to add foods that aren't already in their expansive database. Would recommend it highly to anyone wanting to keep track of their nutrition. Premium version is well worth the price.

I love this app. its really helped me to see how my diet is in terms of calories, I needed to eat a lot more! I didn't realise that i was merly surviving on 1000 calories per day so it really has helped me turn my life and health around. It helps to see the nutrients you need more of too and I needed more calories in general. I am breastfeeding and was losing weight.

Love all the features, but it takes a long time to launch, and long to load pages, and doesn't work offline. I'd also like to modify individual items of a custom food in the diary. Also water intake would be nice. Also widgets to show macros, atats etc. I'll give five stars for offline use, or faster loading. Edit: oh right! there's water in food. congratulations on an amazing app by the way! I'll give it 5 stars anyway, I'll trust that the loading issue will be addressed in time. Thanks!

I dont mind adds on apps when they are reasonably out of the way (eg, at the top or bottom), but the placement in the centre of the screen actually makes this unusable. I have paid for the ad free version now, which I suppose is the idea. I think this is manipulative though, in that its forced on the user.

I love this app.. I have just gone through a lot of calorie reduction and this application helps me control it ..I regret having made a drastic weight loss..Now I try to eat less and more often so that my metabolism returns to normal .. and I hope it will not cause me to gain weight or unnecessary fat.. Thanks to this app, I can now control my calorie intake.. Just one of my requests, enter more food data especially from my country (Malaysia).. It was a bit hard to find my local food

League of it's own I've used a number of calorie counting apps and Chronometer takes the crown. Is a very reasonable price and a user experience that actually makes sense. If you're choosing a calorie tracker, Chronometer just gets it. Small design decisions makes using the app work for you rather than against you, like some of the competitiors. Can not recommend enough!

great app- easy to use, ability to set meals ahead of time, macros counting, love the gold membership which suggests foods to reach your targets for that day, and breakdown of micronutrients. I thought I was getting my daily calcium and vitamins.. tracking my macros and these stats has provided good insights to my food health. also.. like the import recipe feature! worth the money

3.5, i would have rated a 5, but the new mobile UI update is awful, i now only use my phone to add food, i check vitamins and weekly metrics on my computer instead. It also takes twice as many clicks to add food, which is incredibly annoying, terrible update, hope they revert or fix the terrible new UI so i can change my review. in addition the exercise category is sorely lacking and the calories burned doesn't change with your weight as it should.

This is a great app if you want a very comprehensive look at your daily food & nutrition intake. It is helping me to be more accountable with my weight management goals as I get a very accurate reading on intake versus output. And a good look at daily nutrient values as well. There is a bit of a learning curve to understand how to read the data charts, but there is a helpful guide included. The free version is good but the paid version is better- more features and NO ADS🙂

Excellent app. One of a few which became essential for my daily use. I love the option for adding my own recipes or a custom food. I group repetitive meals as a recipe so adding "breakfast" for example saves me time. EDIT in respond to developers' reply: I haven’t noticed the obvious options menu link next to the search bar. It offers the customization I was looking for including sorting and filters. This is awesome!

I don't normally review apps but I'm going to make an exception for this one. I was using one of their competitor apps before making the switch and I couldn't be happier with how things turned out. Cronometer has helped me improve my diet by giving me detailed overviews of what I'm lacking in my daily nutritional intake. Lovely, lovely app.

Great for tracking macros. I've been using Cronometer since going Ketogenic in 2017 to track macros and carbs, which I'd set up a spreadsheet for but that was a pain. Cronometer's recipe feature and the ability to enter custom foods has been really useful with capacity for more nutritional information than most food suppliers provide but the built-in access to a database of analysed food is useful to track vitamin intake. I've found no need to use anything more than the free features.

This app far surpasses any other similar ones I've tried. Having given up on using an app, I tried to track much of the same information on spreadsheets; I had to give up--too time consuming and inaccurate. I'm so happy with this app that I've now paid for the full version because I want as much information as I can get, however I think many users will find that the free level gives them as much information as they're looking for. I definately recommend.

Its well made, but statistics are not usefull for analizing your metabolism or similar. In past years i had used now out of date software called diet organizer which was verry insightful. Detecting deficiencies. Muscle loss or gain over years. Cachexia. What maro is best. How much fiber needed to bring down appetite, caloric intake. Cronometer takes all your info and keeps you kinda dumb. Entering infos into html app also takes more time than with desktop software.

love this app, used it many years. Best app for tracking what l eat and seeing what is in that food, breaks everything down very well. Easy to set macros and see the ratios. l find it helps me lose weight and get healthy. I always feel so much better when l use this app. 😀 For me l break down all my food and put each item from a meal. This app works great with my samsung galaxy fit 2.

Better micronutrient tracking and more flexibility of goals than myfitnesspal, but lacking useful features, like the ability to copy a meal from day to day would be nice (at the moment you can only copy entire days, since the app doesn't break entries into "meals") and also the ability to import ingredients lists from online recipes, which makes importing home cooked meals much easier.

Absolutely fantastic for tracking nutrients, also great for tracking carb/fat/protein ratios. I've lost 5 lbs in one week just by becoming aware of how many carbs I've been taking in thanks to this app. I also have boatloads of energy, and even reduced my cellulite! Also discovered that I have been wasting money on unnecessary supplements, so it's ended up saving me money :) I'm absolutely obsessed with this app.

I've been using this for the past 3 years and it's been great. However, after the last update, the calories for any multi-selected group of food items is miscounted. PLEASE FIX!!! Edit: the newest update seemed to have fixed the issue so the app is back to being fully awesome!

what a great App! You can find almost anything on here if not you can scan the item. I did notice an error in something I scanned and reported it, within days they had responded and fixed the issue. well done to the team! The 4 stars is they don't have all the restaurants and such in Canada. so not the biggest deal.

I made a mistake in my initial review and was corrected by the developers. So I'm changing my rating to 5 start. It works great. Even with just the free membership. Much more intuitive than other tracking apps. I might end up paying for the premium just because the app works so well and I want to support the developers.

Fantastic app that takes most of the work out of keeping track of what you eat. Locking timestamps behind a very steep premium version is the only downside. Note: If the app doesn't save items when you first install, try reinstalling and/or recreating your account. Also support did eventually get back to me, but I had already fixed it.

I have been using this app for a few years, on and off. I am extremely grateful that the free version is enough to plan and track my diet, to create recipes in it, keep track of exercising, and so many other things that I've yet to explore. I also like the fact that you can access the program on the computer, too. This app is a blessing, and I highly recommend it to everyone.

The app doesn't have ads at first and it's free to use, but then ads started popping up and you can close them at first. After a while ads will appear on screen and they cannot be closed and made to go away. Very annoying it didn't just begin with a tenth of the screen covered by an ads, but that's what the free version will end up looking like if you're cool with that. Also it crashes all the time.

Love the custom meal feature so I can, for example, add my breakfast yogurt with fruit and chia seeds all at once! A really nice, easy to use app. Not crazy about the temu ads which often seem to have no way out except to shut down the app and start again. I hope developers will see this and fix it. Otherwise 5 star!

You get a lot of great features for free. Best of all my fitbit syncs to it. I feel like my fitness pal is way over rated app. This app is much better. I like that they show my net carbs. I can keep track of all my macros, vitamins, and minerals. It has very little ads. I got no complaints.

Simple, easy entry - other diet aps get bogged down with clicking through pages or ads before you get to the date every page. Large, reliable database. It's easy to customize total calorie, macro and nutrient goals. Makes it easy to track target nutrients like sodium, iron, and fiber. Can import recipes from webpages. Can make whatever charts you want, and add custom biometrics.

I loathe this app. It is overly complicated, and no matter how many changes I try, it doesn't display the data in a way that isn't overwhelming; difficult to even reset the settings. Wasted money on this app because even with the vast food database for tracking, the over complicated dashboard does not promote compliance with tracking. The help section is a rabbit hole of word salad and the opposite of helpful.

Just came over from Carb Manager. This app is great! Quick to enter food and activity, extensive database, and the design doesn't get in the way. And the Garmin integration is better than other platforms. I just signed up for Gold. Looking forward to it helping me drop quarantine pounds!

Intuitive and straightforward with lots of features in the free version. Unfortunately, nothing works offline, even my password is forgotten if I try to connect without wifi. No calories consumed, no charts, no database, nothing works offline :o/ It should not forget my password when internet is unavailable.

I really like this app as I did when I used Samsung Health years ago... My major complaint and the reason I will not upgrade, is the numbers (all numbers top to bottom) do not match the products labeling even when using the apps scan barcode option. VERY Frustrating... How can I trust any one number if any other number is blatantly wrong? Please update nutritional information more often... If you get the nutrient information from other than the actual product source... the error is on you!

The app is great, it's just really slow. It takes quite a while to load anything when I try to start up the app, or add a food, or delete an entry, etc (like sometimes up to a solid minute or so to load something after one tap, and I'll sometimes have to close it and restart it because it gets stuck). But otherwise it's really useful

It's really sad, this used to be a fantastic app. I used it for years, paid for gold for years. The ads are unbelievable. I don't need the gold service any longer. Cronometer NEEDS to offer a one time fee for an ad free app like they used to. I'm not paying $50/yr to remove these awful intrusive ads. I will most likely be removing all my data and deleting my account.

Very intuitive menus. Easy to use. Like anything... garbage in = garbage out. The upcoming label on.packages is easy to scan and the database has it but, raw foods and whole foods give 5-10x the nutrients info. M7ch better for tracking. Great purchase. Well worth it to not just track macros, but the more important micros.

I love this app, but unfortunately it takes a really long time to load anytime I open the app or try to navigate. I often find I'm closing and opening the app, I've uninstalled and installed it a few times, and tried to figure out if it was something to do with my phone, but still takes a very long time to load, making the app hard to use.

It's easy to use, very intuitive, has many good and free features, lets me input good that's not yet in the very wide database, and helps me get fit and achieve my body fat percentage goals. Only negative thing is it doesn't sync with my mi band, but it can't be perfect for free I guess!

Great app! I use Cronometer daily to help me with general nutrition tracking, and portion control. A few years back I used the web version while I was going keto, and I was able to lose 70lbs. So, thank you Cronometer! I'm giving only 4 stars because of an issue I had with the app over wifi. I had to disable IPv6 on my router or the app will hang for almost 3 minutes on start up every time. Fix that and it's 5 stars!

Love it! Tracks all kinds of importatn nutrients, vitamins and minerals for our body. 😊 Lots of food is already there and tou can create your own recipes. You can set your % of macros and lots more settings. 🙌 I remember times when this app was with no ads and gold acc but yeah I could see it coming 😅 it's very good app.

When it comes to calories and tracking, this application delivers. But it does much more. It has an amazing database of foods, mass in grams and all other ways. The web interface is nice, the Android one is also pretty. Oh, ads are not intrusive at all. All in all it's so near perfection that I find it very difficult to say it isn't.

Helpful for tracking nutrients not found on most food labels like Omega-3 and copper. One thing that would make it more convenient is the option to log other measurements of the foods, especially the whole container (which would help us confirm we were logging the right food). Anyway, great app!

Way easier to use than other apps when it comes to custom recipes & serving portions. I enjoy cooking and am constantly trying new things, but without a keen sense of how my CICO varies from day to day. The flexibility in importing recipes without needing to weigh every little thing before & after cooking ensures a higher likelihood of following thru on tracking. Only thing I'd wave my magic wand to add is a function to import text from pictures of printed recipes i.e. from cookbooks.

So many glitches and poor support meant that I couldn't use the app for months and now I'm uninstalling it in favour of updating it. By the time support got back to me it was irrelevant because I wasn't using the app anymore. It was a lot of adding in my own details and most of the brands I buy weren't in the database and if they were the stats were incorrect. This isn't just some. It was 90% of the time so I had to create my own items with the correct values when that feature became unavailable

the app tracks EVERY nutrient, not just calories, carbs, fats. Very customizable, imports recipes from the web, informs on each nutrient, allows one to see as much info or as little, as wanted. It links to tracker devices via Bluetooth. Supports fasting, keto plans. Stores thousands of food items, many brands as well as fresh, and you make up your own food or recipes. A serious health watching tool.

Female + pregnant! I love that during setup you can select that you are currently pregnant or nursing which will adjust your daily kcal requirements! :) I also love that this syncs with Garmin/ my Garmin watch which is a huge plus! It also shows your daily eating habits in a non judgemental way. It just lays out the nutrients of each food and provides a lot of information in the free version so you can easily track your macros or just simply count your calories.

The only app I've ever used where the UI, Navigation and user input gets incrementally worse. Cumbersome, but thats not all. The design should be focused on less time spent during input, thus making the process of entering, every-meal, every-ingredient, every-time, simple and easy. Spoiler: Its Not. The latest update is by far the worst so far. The UI screams iPhone, quick reference colors are gone, input sec is now the furthest away from your thumbs (top of screen) etc. List goes on. Good luck.

Great for tracking the macros needed for Keto. Excellent data base and ability for custom recipes. Handles net carbs better than other apos I've used. Wish it had a simpler way to track water intake in the diary (vs having to look it up each time). Since I'm using the paid version I did create a water category and am doing it there and in my Fitbit app (where I love the simple water intake tracking!).

Gender issues but a pretty ok app nonetheless. The opening menu uses a gender and sex interchangeably which is weird. And despite having 4 available sexes, only 2 are sexes and the others are 'pregnant' and 'breastfeeding' with no regard for intersex people. It could be easily remideid by asking the user's pronouns. Also the 'not enough info on trans people' seems like a cop out. The app is still hugely useful and has been wonderful otherwise there's just a few things that could use a change.

Trying Cronometer pro, so I can observe 2 of my clients, but I do wish you had ready to use meal plans with ingredients and instructions for everyone to have at their finger tips, other apps available have this feature for their premium users, so it shouldn't be difficult to incorporate into the gold or pro version. Also, meal plans should be for dieting, maintenance and BULKING... not everyone is trying to lose weight, but for gaining healthy muscle mass.

Cronometer is an awesome app for monitoring your nutrition. I love that it has both macro- AND micronutrients and an extensive database of products. I have but one request. Please add deciliters or milliliters for us European users! It's a pain to convert from dl to cups all the time! It has grams, but in baking you are adding ingredients in dl most of the time, rather than grams. Thank you! 😊

Seems quite nice so far. But a really annoying issue is (a) if you're in a place without data you can't enter any food. This problem is solvable by software, it would just understandably take more work from the developers (B) it won't let you autofill the text fields from password management applications, it also disables pasting passwords and usernames. In other words this app doesn't have proper security because of this. I don't understand why developers either disable or don't enable pasting

From the tiring popup ads to the many flaws to the 12 digit, upper and lower case numbers and letters password less than thrilled. My reply: Yes, I could just pay monthly and I could also just go back to my old app with less interrupting ads. As for the password, 4 digits have never failed me for my credit card and 6 digits work perfectly well on high end electronic safe locks. The more difficult the password, the more likely people will store it on their phone, making it LESS secure actually.

Best app I've tried, the database isn't full of junk like in MFP and the search function is way better. I like that it tracks so many nutrients so I can make sure I'm not deficient. Loses 1 star because there's no widget so I can see my calories without opening the app, if they ever make one I'll buy a subscription

INCREDIBLE APP. I have been using cronometer for 12 years, and they have always given the highest quality and thorough information out of any other place. no calorie tracking app has this kind of value without having to pay for a premium. it gives you a complete breakfast of all your daily vitamins, minerals, fats, protein, carbs, water, alcohol consumption; even down to trace minerals like copper. it's amazing. you can also build recipes and save them which is perfect for meal prep, all free.

I was initially impressed with the app; the database is great and I really like the recipe feature. Unfortunately, it wouldn't export data to my FitBit. It uploaded everything fine, but wouldn't download. And without that feature working, I'd have to do double entry so I'll stick with logging my meals into FitBit for now.

First, the food database is dominated by American products, with apparently no option to filter by country. Very well known UK brands can't be found among the noise. Second, the UX is terrible: within sub-menus the back button exits the app without warning; input fields show default values beside the cursor but you cannot delete them, they just vanish when you start typing; the main logo is scaled incorrectly for the first several seconds of using the app and reads "onomet"; etc. etc...

Life-changing app. Currently on free, I am getting all the functions I need. Adding custom food with the option of multiple serving sizes per food, very nice tracking. Have to say really Proper app. Its tons of help for meeting my caloric and specific nutrient intake, all is customizable, goals for kcal, nutrients, vitamins, minerals. It calculates your needs based on age, sex, height, weight, bodyfat, activity, desired goal. Calculations of app match info of many health and bodybuilding sites

This is a great app. Doesn't have the same sort of database of foods as the main competitor does, but that's okay. However I deduct a star for a recurring bug that's really quite frustrating. I'm making a recipe, inputting weights of foods as I go. I scan a food and it says it's new so I go to add it to the data base. After taking a photo, the app closes and restarts - deleting all the measurements in the recipe I was working on.

Cronometer is a highly customisable marco tracker. The food library is extensive, with the ability to create your own custom recipes. The UI is easy to use and flows quite well. The app has tons of tutorials to explain everything to you, this is an excellent feature if you are new to tracking calories and macros. The free app does everything you'll need it to, I cannot comment on the paid side of the app. I think this is a better tracker than MFP.

first of all, I love the variety of macronutrients this app includes for daily life. I also love that you can create your own meals from listed ingredients, and scan barcodes. But this app isn't for me. The "exercise" section is very cluttered and awkward. It's hard to search through; none of them feel accurate enough to what I'm doing. While I appreciate the range of activities, it's hitting everything I don't need. Also, I'm really looking for an app that tracks sugar.

I found a fun detail in this app! Let's say you did your usual smoothie, but with 0 bananas when the recipe calls for 2. You can still add the smoothie to your journal with the recipe shortcut, and then add "-2 medium bananas", to balance the stats! That surprised me, I really expected the app to disallow negative bananas. Turns out the recipe database actually includes accurate nutrient profiles for some other negative foods too, try searching for reverse sear, antipasto or upside down cake.

same what restricted with foods especially vegetables,. site tends to come up with processed prepackaged options first which from New Zealand aren't available. Doesn't scan bar codes and labels easily, even when flat and clear to read. Clunky with syncing to fitbit. wouldn't upgrade to paid version until more user friendly for outside of the States. great to see individual nutrients listed.

I decided to try Chronometer over MyFitnessPal due to cost ....and I am not sure it was a good decision. Deleting ALL diary entries is easily accessible from the top of my diary for the day, but good luck finding where to enter my current weight. In fact, I never found the location to enter that stat, but found it after performing a search. Extremely frustrating. Aside from the issue with that very important feature, the app is acceptable so far. Time & additional familiarity will tell.

Really helpful food log. Saw a vegab blogger using this app. I have been trying to live a vegan lifestyle for the past 2 weeks. This app has helped me see where I need to increase my protein or fat, my carbs are usually maxed out each day. I have added a few items to the food database too. Great app, thank you for developing it.

Cronometer made me realize I didn't need my supplements anymore.. Scan, search and create recipes easily but also track your daily protein, fiber, magnesium, B12 and other things people are consistently deficient in. This is the first app I've cared enough to give a full review because the devs put in the work. Not just good for calories but your macro needs as well. Thank you to the people of this app especially for making these features free.

This is such a cool app for tracking nutrition intake! I was surprised to learn my calcium and magnesium intakes were consistently low. Made it easy to correct a deficit I would never have dreamed I had. Reports are easily customized. U-tube how-to's & free webinars make it easy to learn. Gold membership is a great value.

Easy to use. Doesn't categorise food consumption into meals. Has slightly smaller bank of listed foods than another similar app but adding a custom food is simple. Non-subscribed version does have some adds but nothing to the extent of another app I used that caused me to cancel & delete the app because the adds were so intrusive & obnoxious

Made the switch from MFP after many years due to money-grubbing changes. I wish I'd done so earlier! This app is superior in every way, especially in giving the ability to set keto macros and track net carbs... for free. I may even upgrade eventually, but because I want to, not have to.

I'm currently using this app while breastfeeding my baby with a milk protein allergy. Cutting out dairy products made me worry about certain nutrients and calories missing as a result. This app is so detailed in micronutrients and helped me pinpoint deficiencies. I wanted an app that wasn't centered around weight loss and exercise, since my main goal was maintaining my milk supply while making sure I got my nutrients. It even takes breastfeeding into account on the goals page. Love this app!!

I am on the Keto Diet and Chronometer helps keep me on track with Macros. The app is very easy to use and navigate. The only reason for 4 stars and not 5 is they give you just enough in the free app. If you want a more detailed account you have to pay. Other apps offer more, however I found this one to be the easiest to use and the data is more accurate.

love this app. just wish the food database was larger, especially for restaurants. but I make it work. all the graphs and bars it gives you tickles a part if my brain. it's great. also love that it doesn't give too much advice if any. truly just a tracker and a great one. will be upgrading this month to premium.

Seriously, this is the most advanced, thorough, and user-friendly nutrition tracking app I've ever seen. If you're interested in tracking your macros or just want to ensure you're meeting your basic vitamin & mineral intakes, this provides you with that and SO much more. Where has this been all my life? Found out about this by reading "Thinner, Leaner, Stronger" by Michael Matthews. Upgraded to the paid version (annual), and it is worth every penny. I use both the desktop & app versions.

Love This App! If you are tracking calories or on a specialized diet such as Keto etc this app is the best I've found to break down micronutrients and % within your daily intake. If you do the gold version you can also track your fasting time-frame and do other great options. Another benefit is pulling in data from smart devices bit a new option for Android users is Samsung Health integration as well. Best calorie tracker out there!

So easy to use. I've been using Cronometer for a month to help me stay in a healthy calorie deficit to help me lose my "pandemy belly" & I've already lost 4kg (8.8lbs). Being able to track my calories easily has been amazing. I'm making much better food options & I've started walking daily thanks to this app. I highly recommend it.

Love this app! I was using My Fitness Pal but found it was not detailed enough for me to do keto macros. Not only is Cronometer good for Keto but it has a setting specifically to track Macro for Keto. The details are unmatched for nutrition, minerals and macro nutrients. It works great for me. The only down fall is it does not have a data base as big as My Fitness Pal but it is easy to add foods and the data base is growing. I was able to find most of the food I normally eat on the Cronometer.

Another calorie counting app that locks it's most popular features behind a paywall while providing a subpar mobile experience where you can't easily or quickly change what you're eating. Just buy a notebook and google calories for foods online. It takes a little longer at first but there is enough nonsense with the app that over time it'll even out. And you never have to worry about data loss/breach either, while saving cash. Apps in general seem to be scams relying on laziness now.

I gave it a four because I have issues sometimes with the way food is entered, for example, it will only allow you to select a set amount of grams, but no other measurement. I also think it would ve worthwhile if companies did input the information themselves as new products roll out.

Wonderfully summarizes everything I need to know to have a balanced diet. I love that I can customize which nutrients that I want to focus on! The only problem is that it doesn't always have the foods/exercises logged that I need, but that doesn't effect much because I can just eyeball it.

Great app overall. The app does what it does very well and has a surprisingly large dataset for foods. However, there is a large ad that is at about 20% of the screen and right between two key pieces of information so you can't if ore it easily. Also, sometimes the app will take up to 3-5 minutes to start for some reason. It only happens occasionally. For a free app, it does everything I need and there are no video ads so overall I am very happy with it and the functionality.

Very easy to use. The recipe builder is so easy to use, I have found that grams is a universal measurement in this app, I use my digital scale to help me with that, but it's also on a lot of products. Customer service is very fast, and nutritional information is very accurate. I am not a pro member

Works well for seeing where I might be missing a few nutrients with my whole food plant based diet and helps me to adjust my variety of foods. Much larger food selection than other apps. Immediately imported items but took a day before it started uploading my calories consumed back to Fitbit for some unknown reason.

The most amazing app ever! Tracks all macro AND micronutrients in your food for free. Gives you daily, weekly, monthly, reports on your nutrient intake. ALL FREE. You can pay premium for extra chart features and conveniences. There is an advertisement maybe once every two days, which is fine by me. Thank you!

I understand ads on apps & reasonable fees to get rid of them. This app isn't good enough to require the most invasive ads of any app on my phone (full screen loud ads that force you to watch the entire thing before you can close,) def doesn't offer enough to require a subscription. It won't even let you open it without internet. Edit: every day the unpaid version has more locked features w/ worse ads. Making more money, taking things away. I'll def never buy an app with practices like this.

This app has all the features that I was looking for in caloric tracking. The features include many that other similar apps force users to pay for, such as scanning a bar coded in order to automatically log a food. If I were to recommend any calorie tracking app it would be Cronometer.

Ive used many diet tracking apps through the years, nutritiondata, livestrong, Myfitness pal. Cronometer stands head and shoulders above the rest for ease of use, and informativeness. And I've only ever used the free app. Ill bet the paid version would be even better. Unfortunately, that's not in the works soon

Well pretty silly that if you add a new food you have to wait for it to get added to the database to track it. I said save and it just kept asking me if I wanted emailed when it was available. Well no,, I want to track everything that was put in there. Finally backed out and lost everything entered. Useless app if you can only use existing foods. Time to Uninstall and look for another.

Best food tracking app - period. I love the variety of options but lack of duplicates, and this makes it much easier to enter you daily meals. I love that there are many measurement options (g, tbsp, oz etc.). My favourite features are the fact that you can create your own foods and input information about your homemade goods. Fantastic layout and great colours and it doesn't make feel like I'm filling out a data report (like some other apps) sry I run out of room for review but i ❤️ this app!

The nutrient report page does not update properly. I've added all my foods for the day and it shows the correct values in the highlighted nutrients, but it does not add them properly to the full nutrient report page. E.g. Total calories are 1500, nutrient report showing only 100 calories, and the vitamins/minerals are similarly lacking.

Good app but only in a few days of use, I discovered two mistakes, it had no calcium in a Greek yoghourt and no vitamin c in a orange marmelade. These are just mistakes I discovered by chance....I don't think I can trust their database. I am sorry but even many identical products from NCCDB have totally different nutrition values which makes everything unreliable.

After using Loseit for years, I decided to try out Cronometer. I've switched to a plant based diet and and realized that I needed to track my micronutrients, something that Loseit does not provide. This app really helps me lose weight.... when I take the time to use it! Calorie tracking is super easy, adding activity is also easy. You can add foods that are not already in the app (but you'd be surprised at what is already there). The activity choices could be a bit better (hot yoga, please), but I can usually find something that is similar to what I'm doing. Added bonus is a VERY supportive community of users, many of whom face similar challenges with fitness or weight loss, and reading their posts, along with the replies of support and suggestions is a nice place to go in this increasingly uncivil world.

2.5 years later, I still like this app more than other popular alternatives. I have all my recipes in here and also use it to keep track of what's in my freezer with the saved meals. Update: 5 years later I'm still using FatSecret. There's a premium version available now, and I'm glad they are offering this because I want them to be successful and continue to make improvements. I'm very happy with the results.

I don't see tech support in the app. It would be nice if users could tag nutritional values that may be incorrect so that somebody could review them. I just noticed a discrepancy with McDonald's vanilla iced coffee, with different values per oz between small medium and large. set all three to 32 oz and the large is high in fiber while the small and medium contain no fiber. The app includes no option to report or correct this.

I love this app! It is the fastest, simplest I have used and it gives me detailed information that makes it easy to see where I need to make adjustments in my nutrition, habits, and exercise. Typically, the time it takes to track what I eat daily makes me quit after a few weeka, but this is fast and gives me so much information that it is worth it. I am losing more weight, much more quickly than I have with many other apps and programs.

This is the best app I've found for tracking what I eat. It actually helps me PLAN my meals in advance while making adjustments for the reality checks that happen throughout the day- co-workers bring donuts, I miss a meal because of a meeting, etc. Also, because it's been a lround for a long time, it has a VERY robust food index/library- the biggest I've found. And if it's not there, it's really easy to find parts you're looking for and put them together in a meal! Thanks for the great work.

Great library of food items, many with brand names available. Connects to Samsung Fitness for exercise info, although for some reason it doesn't give you as much credit for calories burned. By tracking my calorie intake, I've lost 16lbs during quarantine, while most people have gained weight. It's the only method that works for real and is manageable because of an app like this one. Forget about the fad diets! I guarantee you are eating way more calories that you think! You really have no idea!

Love this app!!! It's super user-friendly and it has most of the fast food places that I frequent. The huge selection of foods makes it super easy and convenient to make entries. It's actually fun to use this app! I've already lost several pounds in my first 2 weeks, and I'm excited to keep losing the pounds with FatSecret! I don't plan on keeping this app a secret!!!

I use this free app to track all my macros. It's very easy to use. I'm surprised at the number of food sources already available for tracking. When a source isn't already in the database, I can just add it, myself. It allows me to track my daily weight, as well as my carbs, protein, fats, etc., in grams and percentages. I've gotten to the point where I will plan my meal for the next day(s) ahead of time because it's such a time saver. This is exactly what I need as I navigate those last few lbs.

I have been using Fat secret on and off for several years. My most favorite feature is the calendar. Here you can see if you are consuming more calories then you are burning, for me that is more important than sticking to a calorie plan. For the most part foods that I eat and exercise I do are trackable. It would be great if it also tracked measurements.

I'm so glad that I tried this app. Everything is really easy to learn and it's extremely simple to find the food you've eaten from anywhere. It calculates the nutritional facts for you. The only thing I can complain about is the extras they want you to pay for such as keeping up with your water intake, because there are many others apps like this one that include those extras for free. Great app overall though.

Good way to keep track of daily intake of food. It's a bit of a pain the first two weeks because you have to input your food's nutritional info, but once thats done it's fine. Easily searches and finds food (when in their database). One thing, it has never been able to sync with Samsung Health so you won't know your real calorie surplus/deficit as their calorie count default isn't accurate to you (and you can't input the correct count off of watch/app). Hopefully this will change soon.

I love the interface, and the wide variety of ways to view data. This app does more than just count calories. It allows you to think about the quality of the calories, and that is important to me. My only complaint is that when you search for a food, different vslues come up. E. G. Sometimes spinach is 7 calories sometimes 11. I assume it's user input that can't be 100% accurate. Thank you for continually improving it!

This is a pretty good tracker for weight management with extensive food database and reporting options. It loses a star (IMHO) for uneven coverage of units available for food (only cups and grams in some cases, for example) and for lack of fully integrating nutritional advice. For example, the reports don't adjust the percentage of macronutrients recommended based on the reduction in calories. Overall though, it's useful.

Please stop messing with this app. Originally it was perfect, food listed by meal or just a general food search. Then it was changed to, okay here's a few foods you had for this meal and then here's some you've never had for this meal. Whatever, I just adjusted and went with it. Now it's constant pushing to upgrade and no way to get rid of extra buttons for water tracker and custom meals. As the old saying goes, don't fix it if it ain't broke...

Awesome app, much easier to use than FatSecret. I'm really enjoying inputting everything I eat in a day, because finding foods or creating my own, incl. my own meals is so easy! The food library is astonishingly wide. And I love that it's a free app, too! The best feature of all is the daily goals setting and the Nutrients tab, which clearly shows the nutrients breakdown and calories I have left, so it's easy to pick my dinner foods to successfully finish off my daily goal.

Update: Tried using again. Workouts don't subtract from total caloric intake. Whether or not that is correct math, that's what I'm looking for. Otherwise app isn't too bad. I keep trying to find an alternative to MyFitnessPal (too many clicks for every task, ads, etc.) but alas my search continues. I don't need fancy, literally just the following: - accurate food database - easy to use UI - weight loss calculator/daily intake for target weight loss BY TARGET DATE - workouts calculated in.

Although I love this app for food tracking the availability to export, and the lack of ads,. I hate that it won't sync your weight with Google fit. If you're trying to watch what you eat more than likely you're trying to lose weight or gain and with all the Wi-Fi scales these days it would make sense to be able to sync the weight with this app.

as a free user there are limitations to what you can and cannot access but the free version is just as amazing. It helps you keep track of caloric intake and calories burned through exercise-- although they need more options for what exercises you can put in and also to recalibrate it because when I compare it to what a machine says the app is a little further behind. There is also the breakdown for what portion of the meal was fats, carbs, proteins, and so on and so forth. Good online community

Best free calorie tracker right now. Pros: easy food entry interface, extensive catalog of food options, good graphs. Cons: the app name, and the recipe entry system. It requires you to publish your recipe to everyone. I can't just enter that I made 6 servings worth of whatever-was-in-my-fridge soup to get accurate portion entries for me for the next few days, it has to be a permanent formal recipe for everyone to see

It's an easy to use nutrition/ calorie tracker and includes a "social media" style blog where you can offer and receive support. There are presets on the calendar for most major "diets" such as Mediterranean, Keto, and Weight Watchers. Users can track weight, exercise, and nutritional intake. You can also share photos, journal, and food calendar with others, but it is not a requirement.

Works ok, needs some key improvements. For one, you can only add a recipe by visiting the website (not via the app). Another suggestion would be to allow you to easily copy one or more items between meals (or days). Maybe you can already do this, but if so, it's not obvious. My biggest complaint would be how serving sizes are specified. Example: if an item serving is 2tbsp and you used one only 1, you have enter .5. it's awkward & would be easier if sizes were a single unit where applicable.

Used to use my fitness pal, and it became way too buggy, bloated, ad-ridden and just a UI mess to navigate. I found this calorie counter, and while it doesn't have as good of a food finder (yet), it is by far a cleaner, more enjoyable experience. There are some improvements to be made, but this is my new accountability partner, and I recommend!

I love this thing! I've tried others, but this is the only one that let's you adjust your daily calorie goals without jumping through pages of calculations and has an extensive database of food added by real users. I haven't been pestered by any ads, and it seems the only thing lacking in the free version are meal plans, which I don't need. Highly recommend this for anyone serious about keeping track of progress and meeting goals.

Works well for tracking basic metrics and calorie counting. I like the macro chart that it provides as well. However, the 3rd party integrations are somewhat lacking and I find that scanning food items by barcode is hit and miss. It doesn't seem like the barcode database includes as many food items as another app I've used. Still, it works well and I'll be sticking with it for a while.

So far this has been the very best calorie tracking app I've tried. The search feature has found the exact items I was entering without having to wade through tons of inaccurate results, that in-itself sets this app WAY above the others! You have a lot of flexability on entering measurements and you can save meals. The only thing I don't like is that it's incorrect on setting your calorie limit for weight loss, you can however, manually change it so it didn't bother me too much.

Pros: It lets me customize what nutrition info I care most and easily viewed at many levels. I like very much the recipe entry, as I almost eat exclusively home cooked food. And, there are quite a few customize food options. Cons: It syncs with fitbit, but doesn't go the full way. If I go bed at 10, I'd try my best to have forbit updated and open this app right before I go bed, as they suggested. But that's where it stops at the best. So it never captures a whole day.

In general this is a good calorie counting app with access to a lot of pre programed selections from different restaurants and store brand foods. I would love to see a "favorites" option for restaurants or brands to make selecting food easier, but in general this does what I need it to do, sometimes perfectly, other times with a little extra math on my part. Overall I'm happy with it and have continued to use it for some years now

I love this app. It's got a huge database of foods and also has the ability to adjust sizes (for example, instead of 1 serving, you can put .5 for half.) It's very easy to use and I love how it also tracks carbs, protein and fat for me. I need to get better at grams, tho. LOL. Oh, and I also like that you can save meals for easy adding to your diary. For instance, I typically have a bran muffin with either yogurt or a variety of fruits so I save each and can just click on one when I have it.

Not the best. Allows for scanning of barcodes, but because these listings are submitted by users, they are often incorrect. I used the app for about a day and found 3 incorrect items just in that short amount of time! Additionally, the nutrition information is a little sparse. I wanted a wider amount if information on nutrients, and only got basic info. Serving sizes are not easily split, and if there is a way to do so, its not easily found.

I like the app. Really straightforward, easy to navigate, and looking up food and putting in macros is very simple. My only knit picky complaint is not having the ability to have a preferred unit of measurement when punching in food. I always weigh everything in grams, so it can be a tiny bit tedious having to swap cups to grams every time I put something in the food diary. Other than that, it's a solid app for nutrition and weight monitoring.

There's a weird glitch that duplicates items sometimes so I have to go back and delete items from the food log that appear twice. The picture feature didn't accurately capture items. For instance, I took a picture of 2 crackers and it suggested yogurt or sour cream. Don't like that the settings default to Monday as the beginning of the week and there doesn't seem to be a way to change the settings. It would also be nice to easily swipe to another day when logging items.

One of the easier to use calorie counting apps. I chose it over others because it's easy to enter foods, and they don't seem to have as much extra junk in the food searches. It would have been 5 stars except a few things: The app will prompt me to enter my weight for the day multiple times per day, and I wish the food entry was even more flexible when it comes to volume/weight. I don't want "roast chicken" to have multiple entries: one counting by weight and another by volume.

Good interface but searching could be easier. Bar code scanning is awesome but I wish that recent foods had a search, and wasn't broken down by meal. I have a lot of the same thing for lunch or dinner so it's annoying to have to re search everything for dinner when I just had it for lunch. Also, I would like to be able to search all the food I've already had rather than just scrolling.

Great app! East to track what you eat (input) and how much you burn (output). Allows you to lose weight and maintain the loss. Easy to find foods. Selecting from recently eaten is great if you follow routines. It would be helpful if they carried a longer history for those who vary their routine more. Saved meals are huge time savers. I lost 118 pounds while using the app. I'm approaching maintenance mode now; accordingly, I've lost only 5 or so pounds in the last few months.

Have been using since 2014, still a great app, but I have a bug and a feature a request: first the bug- when adding food in the Recently Eaten menu, it won't switch between meals while I'm still in that menu. Example- I add a food to Lunch, it brings up Recently Eaten, I go to the top to switch to the Dinner's Recently Eaten but afterward it still shows all the items from the Lunch's Recently Eaten. Second, the feature request- allow me to tick off or strike through food items. Most of the time, I pre load my foods the day before, and it would really help to keep track of what I actually ate even though I added it to the list.

it really is useful. But if you cook at home BEWARE! The recipe feature is useful when it WORKS! You type in your ingredients and steps and the app tells you how many calories and nutrients it has. Only problem is most of the time the app will randomly DOUBLE a few ingredients, making the calorie count USELESS! If it doubles everything it wouldnt be so bad, but noooo! And you can't edit recipes until they are no longer "under review" mine have been under review for DAYS! i can only eat takeout!

This has been the best of about 5 apps like it that I have tried, 4 of which are considered " best", but come with too many ads or connections to 3rd party businesses. The free version of this app does a great job of allowing you to track progress and keep up with your diet log. Being able to set goals, adjust nutrients, and add to the library of foods is also easy. I usually give apps like this a 3 month trial, this is still month 1, and it is standing strong.

This was a great app. Was pleased for many years. But the latest update ruined it for tacking calories net for intake and exercise. More social, which is a waste. Too bad. I had to roll back and can no longer recommend. I hope the fix with option to interface old version. After a polite educattion, I am pleased to report that there is an "old school" option afterall to keep the style ad features I have gown accustomed to. This returns to being a great app. Thanks FatSecret. (Only it might be wise to let your users know when you make that change, the option switch was not real clear. Thanks. BTW, I used the reports for a dietician to review and counsel me on changes. They were very impessed with the detail. Very helpful. I have come back to this review a year or so later to comment that this remains a great app. My earlier concerns were user error. I am hopeful it will begin to track more micronutrients and present more categories of foods associated with Keto like diets. Still recommending to friends. 😎

New user. I've been researching every nutrition app I can get my hands on, and so far this one seems to have most of the features I am looking for. It also seems pretty user friendly and self explanatory. It doesn't come up as an obvious choice when searching apps. I only found it because I ran across a random blog. I'm glad I kept digging!

This is for the free version only. The only simple and decent calorie tracker (great food database) however, I don't see the real need to separate the food you eat by meals. I mean - who cares? I suppose you could just stuff everything under breakfast to make the app easier to use. It's also too easy to delete food entries. I also don't like how the app doesn't consider net carbs (separate entries for carbs and fiber only). (edit) I was a in a bad mood for my last review lol.

FatSecret has been an invaluable resource on my weight loss and fitness journey. I started teacking my nutrition and activity on the site, and sharing my progress and goals with the community. once I downloaded the app, it made keeping up with everything while away from home much easier. my favorite feature of the app is the ability to scan a barcode and add a fod item to my food diary.

I've used this app several years & loved it. I'm a type 1 diabetic and use it to keep track of calories consumed but more importantly to figure the number of carbs consumed in order to calculate my insulin boluses. I always thought it was a great app. However, I'm not happy with it since the last update. I miss the lists of food categories, restaurants and brands. It takes too long to enter each item. (My son says it hurts to watch me) Bring back the lists, please. I wish I could un-update it.

Love tracking my calories and weight with this app. The only thing I've noticed is when you go to add a food, sometimes there are 2 or 3 options for the same food, with different calorie amounts so I have to double check somewhere else before choosing. There is always the option to add your own entry but it's time consuming. It would be great if they would fact check and delete the incorrect ones! Other than that, I've enjoyed it!

Love this app. The group shared food diary is so helpful that you don't have to enter every food's nutritional value. Alot of times someone has already added it for you. And being able to create your own recipes makes sorting out the calories, carbs, fat, etc so easy. Just put in the ingredients and they calculate it for you..easy peasy! Could not have lost my weight without it.

Great app to track my food and easy to save favorite meals. Quick entry & quick glance to see my fat, calories, etc. It has every food on the planet! Haven't put in workouts yet. Thats next! Update ** i have been intermittent fasting for 3 weeks. This app is so easy i don't get tired of it. Using it for workouts too!

This app has been wonderful when used consistently. I paid big money for a diet service which ended up being a waste of money and I quickly gained it all back. Compared to this, which shows you what you eat and tracks calories as well as macro nutrients. I lost 10 pounds which I hadn't been able to do on my own for 4 years. I discovered I was eating way too much fat. This app is wonderful. I've tried others but this is the best. I rate it a 10!

This App has helped me track my eating habits and curve most of my bad eating choices. By logging everything I consume, it allows me to see my caloric intake as well as the percentage ofcarbs, protien and fats. If you commit to keeping a daily log and keeping track of all you consume the app can really help to hold yourself accountable and make better eating choices. It helps set realistic weight loss goals. Only issue is the food data base, as I have had trouble finding some of my meals.

I think this is the best free calories tracking app on Play. I have tried the other higher ranking app, those have very limited function if you are not paying the expensive subscription. FatSecret has everything you needed, even you are not paying for the premium, while it's not too expensive to pay to support the developers. Although some features (from the web version) is not included in the app, I would advice to use their website together the app. Totally recommended.

It's a good app but I have noticed some discrepancies. I went out to eat and what I got was logged in already to the app but the numbers were all wrong according to the nutritional information the resturant has. I have noticed this with bar codes i have scanned too. The carbs , fat, and protein numbers dont always match what is on the label.

This program is the best I have seen. It covers just about every nutrient one could want except potassium. and phosphrous content. I wish these could be added. These two nutrients are restricted and monitored in kidney failure. This would make this program perfect!!!! As is stands, this program is more inclusive and comprehensive than one I bought for my IPad. So many foods are included. The very best part is being able to shame pictures of foods, recipes, AND to follow individual progress.

It's a good way to log your food. They have several foods in the database and toy can save meals so you can quickly put them in. The only thing I wish they had is the ability to scan an item if you can't find it in the database. If you purchase the premium package you have access to many recipes and plans to try, ie: balanced, keto or low carb. I'm satisfied with this app for logging my food!

Great app, even with the free version! I have always done diets that didn't require calorie counting in the past because I found it tedious, but this makes it simple. My only gripe with the app are that many of the calorie counts of products are 10 or 20 kcal off.
